Topic: The birth of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Christmas Day. After 411-412. 1. One more year the birth of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ has shone for us—and we must celebrate it; in him the truth has sprung from the earth; the day of day has come to our day: let us be glad and rejoice in it. The faith of Christians knows what the humility of such great excellency has given us; The heart of the wicked is kept far from this, for God hid these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to the little ones. Therefore, let the humble possess the humility of God to also reach the height of God with such great help, like a donkey that supports its weakness. Those wise and prudent, on the other hand, when they seek the exalted of God and do not believe the humble, by overlooking this and, consequently, not achieving that due to their emptiness and lightness, their swelling and pride, they remained as if hanging between heaven and earth, in the space proper to the wind. Topic: The birth of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Christmas Day. Between 412 and 416.

1. The day of the Lord's birth is called the date on which the Wisdom of God was manifested as a child and the Word of God, without words, issued the voice of the flesh. The hidden divinity was announced to the shepherds by the voice of the angels and indicated to the wise men by the testimony of the firmament. With this annual festival we celebrate, therefore, the day on which the prophecy was fulfilled: Truth has sprung from the earth and justice has looked down from heaven. The truth that dwells in the bosom of the Father has sprung from the earth to also be in the bosom of a mother. The truth that contains the world has sprung from the earth to be carried by the hands of a woman. The truth that incorruptibly feeds the blessedness of the angels has sprung from the earth to be suckled by breasts of flesh. The truth for which heaven is not enough has sprung from the earth to be placed in a manger. For whose sake did such great excellency come with such humility? Certainly, it did not come for his good, but for ours, provided we believe. Wake up, man; For you, God became man! Arise, you who sleep; rise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you.

You could never be free from sinful flesh if he had not taken the likeness of sinful flesh. An endless misery would dominate you if this mercy had not taken place. Let us celebrate with joy the arrival of our salvation and redemption. Let us celebrate this holiday in which the great and eternal day from that great and eternal day came to this our day, brief and temporary. He became for us righteousness, sanctification and redemption, so that, as it is written, whoever glories may glorify in the Lord. So that we do not resemble the arrogance of the Jews, who, ignoring God's justice and wanting to establish their own, did not submit to God's, after having said the truth has sprung from the earth, he immediately added and justice has looked down from heaven. With this purpose: so that she would not arrogate mortal weakness to herself; so that he would not say that it was his, and believing that man justified himself, that is, that being righteous was his own work, he would reject the justice of God. The truth, then, has sprung from the earth: Christ, who said I am the truth, was born of a virgin. And justice has looked down from heaven: man does not justify himself, but is justified by God, if he believes in him from whom he was born. The truth has emerged from

the earth: The Word became flesh. And justice has looked down from heaven: Every optimal gift and every perfect gift comes from above. The truth has sprung from the earth: the flesh, from Mary. And justice has looked down from heaven: Man can receive nothing that is not given to him from heaven. 3. Therefore being justified by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access to this grace in which we live and rejoice in the hope of the glory of God. And this does not happen in successive stages, as if the sermon that is being preached first entered you and then came out, as a condition to be able to enter another, but rather it reaches everyone at the same time and in its entirety to each one. And if memory could retain it in its entirety, as you all came to hear it all, you would still return, each one of you taking it in its entirety. How much more the Word of God, by whom all things were made, and which, remaining in itself, renews them all; which is neither limited by space, nor extended in time, nor varies according to the long or short duration of the syllables, nor is it woven with sounds, nor does it end with silence! How much more could this great and unequaled Word, once the body had been assumed, fertilize the mother's womb without moving away from the Father's womb; manifest from the former to the eyes of men and from the latter illustrate the minds of the angels; go out to the towns from the first and fill the skies from the second; in one to become a man and in the other to make men! 23. Being the son of God, he became the son of man, assuming human nature in its fullness without the divine nature disappearing. Well, not because it was said: The Word was God and The word became flesh, it must be understood that the Word became flesh in such a way that it ceased to be God, whereas Immanuel, that is, God with us, was born in the flesh that took the Word. The word we carry in our hearts becomes a voice when we utter it through our mouths; but that does not mean that the former is transformed into the latter, but rather, remaining intact, it is assumed by the latter, through which it goes outside, so that the intelligible content remains inside and the sound is heard outside; what is now uttered in sound had previously sounded in silence. Thus, when the word becomes a voice, it is not transformed into a voice, but, remaining in the light of the mind and assuming the voice of the flesh, it goes out to meet the listener, without abandoning the one who thinks it. I am not referring to the voice itself, whether of the Greek or Latin language or any other that is thought in silence, but to the reality that has to be expressed and is prior to all diversity of languages; In a certain way, it is still naked in the heart of the person who thinks it, and in order for it to come out, it is clothed with the voice of the speaker. With everything, however, both things, what is thought with intelligence and what sounds when spoken, are mutable and dissimilar things; none will remain: neither the first when you forget it nor the second when you shut up. Instead, the Word of the Lord remains forever unchangeable.

There is nothing strange in the fact that no thought, no human word, is sufficient when we prepare to praise the Son of God as he is with the Father, co-eternal and equal to him, the son in whom all things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, were created; Word of God and God, life and light of men. For how can our tongue worthily praise someone who cannot yet see our heart, the only eye capable of seeing it provided it is purified from all evil and heals its own weakness? Then, those who have a clean heart will be happy, because they will see God. There is nothing strange, I repeat, that we do not find words to say the only Word in which it was said that those of us who have to say something about it exist. Nor does man create words in the same way that he is created by the Word, since neither did the Father beget his only Word in the same way that he made all things through the Word. Topic: The birth of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Christmas Day. Between 391 and 400.

1. Our Lord Jesus Christ, who existed together with the Father before being born of the mother, not only chose the virgin from which he was to be born, but also the day on which he was to be born. Even men, subject to mistakes, frequently choose dates, one to plant a vineyard, another to build, another to go on a trip and sometimes even to get married. By doing so he hopes that the fruit resulting from the action will develop happily. But no one can choose the day of their birth. He, on the other hand, could choose both, because he could create both. And he did not choose the day like those who vainly make the fate of men depend on Christum portabis, non etrabis ambulans per viam: sedet supra te via. Meministis asellum illum adductum ad dominum? Nemo erubescat, us sumus. Sedeat supra nos domínus, et quo vult nos vocet. Iumentum ip sius sumus, ad Ierusalem imus. Ipso sedent non premimur, sed elevamur; ipso ducente non erramus: ad illum imus, per illum imus, non perimus.

The Latin word we translate as "mature" is iuvenis. In no way can it be translated here by "young" in the usual sense of the term. Augustine usually uses the term in this meaning more often. Thus, for example, speaking of the work of Trinidad, he says in letter 174 to Aurelius, bishop of Carthage, that he began the work when he was iuvenis. Since he started it around 400, he was about forty-six years old at the time. In Commentaries on Psalms 127:5 he places the iuventus immediately before senectus or old age, which began at sixty years of age. Qui non ex vobis natus est, vobis natus est. Verumtamen si verbi eius memineritis, sicut meminisse debentis; estis etiam vos matres eius, quia voluntatem facitis Patris eius. Ipse enim dixit: Quicumque facit voluntatem Patris mei, ipse mihi frater et sóror et mater est (Mt 12,50). Exsult yourself, viduae Christi; qui fecundam fecit virginitatem, illi vovistis continentiae sanctitatem. Exsulta etiam, castitas nuptialis, omnes fideliter viventes cum coniugibus vestris: quod amisistis in corpore, in corde sérvate. Ubi iam non potest a concubitu caro integra, sit in fide virgo conscientia, secundum quam virgo est omnis Ecclesia. In Maria Christum pía virginitas peperit: in Anna Christum viduitas parvum grandaeva cognovit: in Elisabeth Christo coniugalis castitas et anilis fecunditas militavit. So that no one would despise the truth for having sprung from the earth, since as a husband he came out of his nuptial bed, that is, from the womb of the virgin, where the Word of God was united in an ineffable consortium to the human creature; so that no one would despise her, I repeat, and, despite the admirable nature of her birth, her doctrine and her works, because of the similarity of sin, believe that Christ was nothing more than a man, after having said: Like a bridegroom leaving his marriage bed, leapt like a giant ready to travel his path, he added next: His departure from the extremity of heaven. When you hear: the truth has sprung from the earth, think that it was his condescension, not the necessity of his condition; that it was mercy, not misery. To spring from the earth, truth came down from heaven. To leave his marriage bed, the bridegroom first made his exit from the extremity of heaven. That is the reason why he was born today; the shortest day of any on earth, but from which, however, the others increase. So, he who lowered himself and raised us up, chose the shortest day, but the one from which the light increases. With his very arrival, without speaking, but with a kind of great cry, he exhorts us to be rich in the one who became poor for us; that we may receive freedom in him who took the form of a servant for us; that we may possess in heaven the one who for us has sprung from the earth.

3. Let us all, then, in unity of spirit, with chaste minds and chaste desires, celebrate the day of the Lord's birth; day in which the truth has sprung from the earth, words with which I began this sermon. What appears in the same psalm below has also already been fulfilled. In fact, justice has also looked down from heaven, since he who sprang from the earth, that is, he who was born of the flesh, came from heaven and is above all. It has been fulfilled, without a doubt, once he ascended to the Father. He himself refers to this justice in his own words when he promised the Holy Spirit: He, he says, will accuse the world of sin in relation to justice and judgment. Of sin, because they did not believe in me; regarding justice, because I am going to the Father, and you will no longer see me. Behold the justice that has looked down from heaven. Veritas de terra, iustitia de cáelo. Die minimum anni cur natus Christus.—Omnes ¡taque unanimouss, castis mentíbus et affectibus sanctis, diem Natalis Domini celebremus; quo die, sicut istum sermonem exorsi sumus: Veritas de terra orta est. Iam enim et quod in eodem psalmo sequitur, factum est. Nam ille qui de terra ortus est, hoc est, de carne natus est, quia de cáelo venit, et super omnes est (cf. lo 3,31); procul dubio cum ascendit ad Patrem, etiam iustitia de cáelo prospexit. Hanc enim iustitiam verbis suis ipse commendat, promittendo Spiritum sanctum: Ipse, inquit, arguet mundum de peccato, et de iustitia, et de iudicio. De peccato quidem, quia non crediderunt in me: de iustitia, quia ad Patrem vado; et iam non videbitis me (lo 16,8-10). Haec est iustitia, quae de cáelo prospexit. A summo enim cáelo egressio eius, et occursus eius usque ad summum caeli. Ne vero quisquam contemneret veritatem, 4 See supplementary note 4: The Church, virgin and mother p.783,

quia de terra orta est, cum sicut sponsus processit de thalamo suo, id est, de uterus virginali, ubi Verbum Dei creaturae humanoe quodam inelfabili coniugio copulatum est: ne hoc ergo quisquam contemneret, et quamvis mirabiliter natum, et dictis factisque mirabilem, tamen propter similarityinem carnis peccati nihil amplius Christum quam hominem crederet, cum dictum esset: Tanquam sponsusprovens de thalamo suo, exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam; continuous subiunctum est: A summo cáelo egressio eius (Ps 18,6.7). Quod ergo audis, Veritas de terra orta est, dignatitio est, non conditio; mercy is, not misery. Veritas ut de terra oriretur, de cáelo descendit: sponsus ut de thalamo suo proceedet, a summo cáelo egressio eius. Inde est quod hodie natus est, quo die minor dies nullus in terris, a quo tamen increment dies sumunt. Qui ergo inclinatus est, et nos erexit, minimum elegit diem, sed unde lux crescit: ipso suo tali adventu, nos etiam tacitus tanquam sonitu magni clamoris exhortans, ut qui pauper propter nos factus est, in illo divites esse discamus; qui propter nos formam servi accepit, in illo libertatem accipiamus; who propter nos de terra ortus est, in illo caelum possideamus.
The birth of the Lord
Topic: The birth of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Christmas Day of the year 410.

1. When the gospel was read to us, we heard the words by which the angels announced to the shepherds the birth of the Lord Jesus Christ from a virgin: Glory to God in the heavens, and peace on earth to men of good will. Words of celebration and congratulation not only for the woman whose womb had given birth to the child, but also for the human race, for whose benefit the virgin had given birth to the Savior. In truth, it was worthy and completely convenient that she who had procreated the lord of heaven and earth and had remained a virgin after giving birth, should see her birth celebrated not with human celebrations of some little women, but with the divine songs of praise of an angel. Let us, then, say it too, and let us say it with the greatest joy that is possible; we who do not announce his birth to shepherds, but celebrate it in the company of his sheep; Let us also say, I repeat it again, with a heart full of faith and with a devout voice: Glory to God in the heavens, and on earth peace to men of good will. Let us meditate with faith, hope and charity these divine words, this song
IN NATALI DOMINI, X

1. Angelorum vocem, per quam Dominus Iesus Christus natus Virginis partu, pastoribus nuntiatus est, cum Evangelium legeretur, audi mus: Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis (Luke 2:14). Festa vox et gratulatoria, non uni feminae, cuius uterus prolem ediderat; sed human generi, cui Virgo pepererat Salvatorem. Dignum enim erat, [1014] et hoc prorsus decebat, ut ei fetae quae Dominum caeli et terrae procreaverat, et post editum fetum integra manserat, non mulierculae humanis solemnitatibus, sed Angelí dívinis laudibus, fetalia celebraent. Dícamus ergo et nos, et quanta possumus cum exsultatione dicamus, qui non pecorum pastoribus eum natum nuntiamus, sed eius Natalitia cum eius ovibus celebramus: dicamus, inquam, et nos fideli corde, devota voce: Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis. Et haec verba divina, has Dei laudes, hoc angelicum gaudium, quanta valemus consideratione perspectum, fide et spe et caritate
of praise to God, this angelic joy, considered with all the attention of which we are capable. Just as we believe, hope and desire, we too will be “glory to God in

the heights" when, once the spiritual body has been resurrected, we are taken to meet Christ in the clouds, provided that now, while we are on earth, we seek peace with good will. Life in the heights certainly, because there is the region of the living; good days also there where the Lord is always the same and his years do not pass. But whoever loves life and wishes to see good days, restrain his tongue from evil and let his lips not speak lies; turn away from evil and do good, and thus become a man of good will. Seek peace and pursue it, for peace on earth to men of good will. 2. If you say, oh man, that wanting good is in you, but you cannot achieve it; that you delight in the law of God according to the inner man, but see another law in your members that opposes the law of your mind and that takes you captive in the law of sin that resides in your members, take hold in your good will and exclaim with these words: Woe to me! Who will free me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord. He is, in fact, peace on earth for men of good will after the war in which the flesh has desires contrary to those of the spirit, and the spirit contrary to those of the flesh, so that you do not do what you want, because he is our peace, who made both of us puemeditemur. Sicut enim credimus et speramus et desideramus, erimus et nos gloria in excelsis Deo, cum resurgente corpore spirituali rapti fuerimus in nubibus obviousm Christo: si moda cum in terra sumus, pacem cum bona volúntate sectemur. In excelsis quippe vita, quia ibi regio vivorum; et ibi dies boni, ubi Dominus idem ipse est, et anni eius non deficiunt. Quisquís autem vult vitam, et diligit videre dies bonds, cohibeat linguam suam a malo, et labia eius non loquantur dolum; declinet a malo, et faciat bonum: et ita sit homo bonae voluntatis. Et quaerat pacem, ac sequatur eam (cf. Ps 33:13-15): quia in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis. 2. Quod si dicis, o homo: Ecce velle adiacet mihi, perficere autem bonum non invenio; et condelectaris legi Dei secundum interiorem hotninem, vides autem aliam legem in membris tuis repugnantem legi mentís tuae, et captivum te ducentem in lege peccati quae est in membris tuis; persiste in bona volúntate, and exclaims quod sequitur: Miser ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius? Gratia Dei, per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum (Rom 7:18-25).

Ipse est enim pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis, post bellum in quo caro concupiscit adversus spiritum, et spiritus adversus carnem; ut non quae vultis illa faciatis (Gal 5,17): quoniam ipse est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum (Eph 2,14). Persistat igitur bona voluntas adversus concupiscentias malas, et

blos one. Therefore, let good will persist in you against evil desires, and in your perseverance implore the help of the grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord. If the law of your members of flesh opposes you, if you even already have it captive, implore help, do not trust in your strength, and at least, when you are tired, do not disdain to confess your weakness, for he will come to those who said he saw that they already believed in him: If you continue in my word, you will truly be my disciples; you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. The truth will come and free you from the body of this death. This is why the truth, whose birth we celebrate, has sprung from the earth: to be peace on earth for men of good will. Well, who will be capable of wanting and being able if he who, with his vocation, gave us love, does not help us with his inspiration so that we can do it? 1 At all times his mercy warned us so that we who did not want to be called and ask for power what we want. Let us say to him, then: I have sworn and determined to keep the judgments of your justice. I have determined it; Since you commanded it, I promised obedience; but I see another law in my members that opposes the law of my mind and takes me captive to the law of sin that resides in my members; I am humiliated, Lord, everywhere; give me life, according to your word. Behold, the will is in me; by persistens imploret auxilium gratiae Dei, per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum. Repugnatur illi a lege membrorum carnalium, et ecce iam etiam captivatur: imploret auxilium, non fidat viribus suis; et saltem fessa, non dedignetur esse confessa. Aderit enim qui dixit ei quos iam videbat credentes in eum: Si permanseritis in verbo meo, veré discipuli mei eritis; et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos (lo 8,31-32). Aderit et liberabit veritas de corpore mortis huius. Ideo quippe Veritas, cuius Natalitia celebramus, de terra orta est (Ps 84,12), ut sit pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis. Nam quis idoneus est velle et posse, nisi inspiring adiuvet ut possimus, qui vocando praestitit ut velimus? Quia ubique miseri[1015]cordia eius praevenit nos, ut vocaremur qui nolebamus, et ut impetremus posse quod volumus. Dicamus ergo ei: luravi, et statui custodire iudicia iustitiae tuae.

Statui quidem, et quia imperasti, promisi oboedientiam: sed quoniam video aliam legem in membris meis repugnantem legi mentís meae, et captivum me ducentem in lege peccati, quae est in membris meis; humiliatus sum usquequaque, Domine, vivifica me secundum verbum tuum. Ecce velle adiacet mihi; ergo voluntary oris mei approba, Domine (Ps 118,106-108); ut fiat pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis. Dicamus ista, et si qua alia suggerit If, as seems to be the case, this statement is directed against the Pelagians, then it is difficult to maintain the date proposed by A. Kunzelmann for the present sermon, that is, Christmas of the year 410 (Die Chronologie der Sermones des hl. Augustinus: MA I p.4him). The beginning of the controversy was marked by the problem of the origin of mortality and the baptism of children as a consequence of the propaganda of Celestio in Carthage. It must be later.
The birth of the Lord

Therefore, Lord, approve the desires of my mouth, so that there may be peace on earth for men of good will. Let us say these things and any other things that piety, instructed by the holy readings, may suggest to us, so that the repeated celebration of the Lord's virgin birth may not be fruitless, but that, initiated into good will, we may merit the perfection of full charity, also spread in our hearts not by ourselves, but by the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.

CAPOT I.—1. Nativitas Christi duplex. Dies nativitatis Christi et loannis.—Audite, filii lucis, adopti in regnum Dei; fratres carissimi, audite; audite, et exsultate, iusti in Domino, ut vos rectos possit decere laudatio (cf. Ps 32,1). Audite quod nostis, recolite quod audistis, amate quod creditis, praedicate quod amatis. Sicut annivetsarium celebramus hunc diem, sic buic diei debitum exspectate sermonem. Natus est Christus, Deus de Patre, homo de matre. De Patris immortalitate, de matris virginitate. From Patre sine matre, from matre sine patre. De Patre sine tem

The Father's lie is the beginning of life; in the mother's, the end of death; born of the Father, order every day; born of the mother, consecrate this day. He sent ahead a man, John, who was born just when the days begin to decrease; and he himself was born when the days begin to increase, symbolizing in this what John himself says: It is fitting that he increase and that I, on the other hand, decrease 1. Human life must decrease in itself and increase in Christ, so that those who live no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and rose again for all, and each one of us can repeat what was said by the Apostle: I live, but not I, but it is Christ who lives in me. Therefore, it is appropriate that he grow and that I, on the other hand, decrease. 2. All his angels praise him as he deserves, of whom he is eternal food and whom he gives life to with incorruptible food. He is, in fact, the Word of God, by whose life they live, by whose eternity they always live, and by whose goodness they live in perpetual happiness. They praise him as he deserves, as God next to God, and give glory to God in the highest. We, however, his people and the sheep of his flock, to the extent of our weakness, reconciled by good will, deserve peace. The same angels correspond to those words that we hear today, and that they uttered full of joy when the Savior was born to us: Glory to God in the highest, and in

peace to men of good will on earth. If they praise him worthily, let us also praise him obediently. They are their messengers, we are their sheep. In heaven he filled the table for them, on earth he filled our manger. He fills the table of angels, because in the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and also fills our manger, because the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. So that man could eat the bread of angels, the creator of the angels became man. They praise him by living, we by believing; them enjoying, we asking; them taking, we searching; them entering, us knocking at the door. 3. What man will know all the treasures of wisdom and science hidden in Christ and hidden in the poverty of his flesh? Although he was rich, he became poor for us, so that we might become rich through his poverty. He assumed mortality and consumed death, manifesting himself in poverty; but he did not lose the riches left aside, but rather promised them, although deferred. How great is his sweetness, hidden from those who fear him, and manifested in those who put their hope in him! Our knowledge is partial until fullness comes. To enable us to attain it, he who was equal to the Father in the form of God, made like us in the form of a servant, restores us in the likeness of God. Becoming the son of man, the only son of God, he becomes sons

Verbi visione post hanc vitam satiabimur. — Quis enim hominum omnes thesauros sapientiae et scientiae noverit in Christo occultos, atque in paupertate carnis eius absconditos? Quia propter nos pauper factus est, cum dives esset, ut illius paupertate ditaremur (2 Cor 8,9). Cum enim mortalitatem assumeret, mottemque consumetet, in paupertate se otendit; sed divitias dilates promisit, non ablatas amisit. of God to many sons of men, and by nurturing, through the visible form of a servant, those who are slaves, he makes them free to see the form of God. We are children of God and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when he appears, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is. Indeed, why do we speak of treasures of wisdom and science, of divine riches, if not because they are enough for us? And why such abundant sweetness if not because it satisfies us? So show us the Father, and it is enough for us. In a certain psalm, any of us, or one who speaks in us or through us, says: I will be satisfied when your glory is revealed. He and the Father are one thing, and whoever sees him also sees the Father. Therefore the Lord of power is the same king of glory. If he converts us, he will show us his face, we will be saved, we will be satisfied and we will have enough. 4. Let our hearts therefore say to him: I have sought your face; I will seek your face, Lord; do not turn your face away from me. Let this be your answer: He who loves me keeps my commands; Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father and I will also love him and show myself to him. Without a doubt, those to whom he said this were seeing him with their eyes and listening with their ears to the sound of his voice, and in their human hearts they thought that he was just a man; But to those who loved him he promised to show them himself, that is, what eye has never seen, nor ear heard, nor has it reached the heart of man. Until this happens, until he shows us what is enough for us, until we drink and are satisfied with him, Dei, multos filios hominum facit filios Dei; et nutritos servos per visibilem formam servi, perficit liberos ad videndam formam Dei. Filii enim Dei sumus, et nondum appa[1017]ruit quid erimus. Et scimus quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est (1 lo 3,2). Nam qui sunt illi sapientiae scientiaeque thesauri, quae illae divitiae divinae, nisi quia sufficiunt nobis? Et quae illa multitudo dulcedinis, nisi quia satiat nos? Oslende ergo nobis Vatrem, et sufficit nobis (lo 14.8). Et in quodam psalmo quidam ex nobis, vel in nobis, vel pro nobis, ait illi: Satiabor, dutn manifestabitur gloria tua (Ps 16,15). Ipse autem et Pater unum sunt (cf. lo 10,30): et qui ipsum videt, videt et Patrem (cf. ibid., 14,9). Ergo Dominus virtutum, ipse est rex gloriae (Ps 23:10). Convertens nos, ostendet nobis faciem suam; et salvi erimus (cf. Ps 79,4), et satiabimur, et sufficiet nobis. CAPUT IV.—4.

Conclusion.—Dicat itaque illi cor nostrum: Quaesivi vultum tuum; vultum tuum, "Domine, requiram; ne ventas faciem tuam a me (Ps 26,8.9). Et responderat ipse cordi nostro: Qui diligit me, mandata mea custodit: et qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo; et ego diligam eum, et ostendam me ipsum illi (lo 14,21). Videbant utique eum oculis illi quibus hoc dicebat, et sonum vocis eius auribus audiebant, et humano corde hominem cogitabant: sed quod oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit, eumdem ipsum se promittebat ostendere diligentibus se (cf. 1 Cor 2:9).

1. Our Lord Jesus Christ, son of God and son of man, as born of the Father without a mother, created every day; as born of a mother without a father, he made this day sacred. In his divine birth he is invisible, visible in the human, and nobis quod sufficiat nobis, doñee eum fontem vitae potemus et satiemur; interim dum ambulantes per fidem peregrinamur ab eo, dum esurimus et sitimus iustitiam, et formae Dei pulchritudinem ineffabili ardore desideramus, formae servi Natalem devoted gift celebremus. Nondum contemplan possumus quod genitus est ante luciferum a Patre, frequentemus quod nocturnis horis est natus ex virgine. Nondum capimus, quod ante solem permanet nomen eius (cf. Ps 71,17), agnoscamus in solé positum tabernaculum eius. Nondum contuemur Unicum permanentm in Patre suo, recordemur sponsum compram de thalamo suo (cf. Ps 18,6). 1. Nativitas Christi duplex, utraque inenarrabilis.—Filius Dei idemque filius hominis Dominus noster Iesus Christus, sine matre de Patre natus, creavit omnem diem; sine patre de matre natus, consecravit hunc diem; divina nativitate invisibilis, humano visibilis, utraque mirabilis. Proinde quod de illo propheta praedixit: Generationem eius quis enar-
The birth of the Lord

in both admirable. Consequently, it is difficult to affirm to which of the two births what was predicted by the prophet refers: His generation, who will narrate it?: whether to the one in which he was never unborn being coeternal with the Father, or to this one, in which he was born in time after having made the mother in which he was going to be made. If it refers to the one in which someone who has always existed was born forever, who will narrate how the light was born from the light, both being one light; How was God born from God, without the number of the gods increasing? How can we say that he was born, using the verb in the past tense, if in that birth time does not pass - which would make it belong to the past -, nor does it precede - which would allow us to speak of the future -, nor is it present - in that it is still taking place, and, therefore, is not yet complete? Who, then, will narrate this birth, if the object of the narration remains outside of time, while the narrator's word, on the other hand, passes in time? And also, who will narrate his birth from a virgin, if his carnal conception was not carried out through the flesh, if his nativity in the flesh granted fertility to the one who created him, without taking away the virginal integrity of the one who gave birth to him? Whether we talk about one or the other, or both at the same time, their generation, who will narrate it? ' 2. He is the Lord our God; He is the mediator between God and men, man our Savior, who, as born of the Father, also created his mother, and, created from the mother, also glorified the Father; As for born without rabit birth? (Is [1018] 53,8) de qua potius dictum sit, iudicare difficile est; utrum de illa ubi nunquam non natus coaeternum habet Patrem, an de ista ubi aliquando natus, in qua ièret, iam fecerat matrera: utrum de illa ubi semper natus est, qui semper erat; quis enim enarrabit quomodo natum sit lumen de lumine, et unum lumen utrumque sit? quomodo natus sit Deus de Deo, nec deorum numeras creverit? quomodo velut de re transacta dicatur quod natus est, cum tempus in illa nativitate nec transierit, quo praeterita esset; nec praecesserit, quo future esset; nec praesens fuerit, quasi adhuc ieront, et perfection non esset? Hanc ergo generationem quis enarrabit, cum id quod enarrandum est supra tempora maneat, sermo autem enarrantis in tempore transeat?

of a woman, he is the only son of the Father, and as born without a man's embrace, he is the only son of his mother. He is the most beautiful of the sons of men, son of Saint Mary, husband of the holy Church, which he made like his mother. In fact, for us he made her a mother and for himself he kept her a virgin. The Apostle refers to her: I have united you with a single man to present you to Christ as a chaste virgin. This is the day on which the creator of the world came into the world; in which he became present in the flesh who is never absent because of his power. Indeed, he was in the world and came to his house. It was in the world, but hidden from the world, because the light shone in the darkness, and the darkness did not welcome it. He came, therefore, in the flesh to cleanse the vices of the flesh; He came in medicinal soil to cure our inner eyes with it, which had blinded our outer earth; so that, once healed, we who were once darkness may be light in the Lord, and the present light will no longer shine in the darkness for those who are absent, but will appear clearly to those who look at it. For this purpose the bridegroom emerged from his wedding bed and jumped for joy like a giant ready to walk his path. Beautiful as a husband, strong as a giant, worthy of love and fear, severe and serene; beautiful for the good, hard for the bad; remaining in the bosom of the Father, he filled the womb of the mother. His generation, who will narrate it? 'Who will worthily narrate God in the act of generating? Who will worthily recount the birth of a virgin? The first happens without a day, the second on a precise day; both things above human estimation and cause for great admiration. Consider the first birth: In the beginning there was the "Word," and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Whose Word? From the Father himself. What Word? The Son himself. The Father never existed without the Son, and yet he who never existed without the Son begat the Son. He begat Him, but he had no beginning. He has no beginning who was begotten without a beginning. And yet he is a son and is begotten. He can say man: "How is it begotten, if it has no beginning? If it has been begotten, it has a beginning, and, if it has no beginning, how has it been begotten?" 2 How I ignore it. Do you ask a man how God was created? Your question puts me in trouble, but I turn to the prophet: His generation, who will narrate it? Come with me to this human birth, come with me to this birth in which he emptied himself by taking the form of a servant. Perhaps we can understand, at least, this one; Maybe we can talk at least something about him. Indeed, who will understand this: who, existing in the form of God, did not consider it a depredation to be equal to God? Who can understand it? Who can have worthy thoughts about it? What mind will dare to scrutinize it? What language will dare to pronounce it? What intelligence can understand it?
Topic: The birth of the Lord. Location: Hippo. date:
Christmas Day. After the year 396.

1. Today the festive day of the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ has shone for us. Day of birth: the day was born on it. And today precisely, because from today the days grow. There are two births of our Lord Jesus Christ: one divine, the other human, and both admirable; he without a woman who was a mother, this one without a man who was a father. What was said by the prophet Isaiah can refer to both births: gigas ad currendam viam (cf. Ps 18:6). Speciosus ut sponsus, fortis ut gigas, amabilis et terribilis, severes et serenus, pulcher bonis, asper malis, manens in sinu Patris, im[1019]plevit uterum matris. In quo thalamo, id est, Virginis uterus, natura divina sibi copulavit humanom: ubi Verbum caro factum est pro nobis, ut a matre proceedens, habitaret in nobis (cf. lo 1,14); ut ad Patrem praecedens, ubi habitemus praeparet nobis. Hunc ergo diem laeti solemniter celebremus; et aeternum diem, per eum qui nobis aeternus in tempore natus est, fideliter exoptemus.

How can it be understood that someone looks at the works and does not look for their creator? You contemplate the earth covered with fruits, the sea full of its own animals, the air full of birds; You observe how the firmament shines with the stars, etc., and do you not look for the author of such a great work? But you tell me: "I see things, but I don't see him." So that you could see those things he gave you the eyes of the body; so that you could see him he gave you his mind. Indeed, you do not see the soul of man either. But as through the movements and government of the body you understand the existence of a soul that you do not see, so also from the government of the entire world and of the souls themselves you must understand the existence of the creator. to all Greeks and other peoples. But there is no idolatry greater and more superstitious than that of the Egyptians, since it was Egypt that filled the world with figures such as those indicated below by the Apostle. Thus, after having said: In the likeness of the image of corruptible man, he added: and of birds, quadrupeds and reptiles. Have you seen, brothers, in other temples an idol with the head of a dog or a bull, or figures of the other irrational animals? These idols are typical of the Egyptians. The Apostle covers both types when he says: In the likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, quadrupeds and reptiles. For this reason God gave them over to the desires of their hearts, to uncleanness, so that in themselves they would fill their own bodies with dishonor. These evils are the result of the evil of their pride. And these sins, since they come from pride, are not only sins, but also tortures. In fact, when it says: God handed them over, it appears that doing so is retribution for some sin. Who exchanged the truth of God for a lie. What does it mean: they changed God's truth for a lie? In the likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, of quadrupeds, and reptiles. And so that none of them should say: "I do not worship the simulacra, but what they signify," he immediately added: And they worshiped them, and served the creature instead of the creator. Understand this correctly. They either worship a simulacrum or a creature. He who worships the simulacrum turns the truth of God into a lie. The sea, for example, is something true; Neptune 2, on the other hand, is a lie created by man: so, then, has God's truth become a lie, because the sea was made by God, nabilium figmenta? Haec enim idola aegyptiorum sunt. Utrumque enim genus complexus apostolus ait: In similarityinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis et uolucrum et quadrupedum et serpentium. Propterea tradidit illos deus in desideria cordis eorum in immunditiam, ut contumeliis afficiant corpora sua in semetypsis (ib., 24). Haec mala eorum, ex impietate supetbiae sunt. Ista uero peccata quia de superbia sunt, non solum peecata sed etiam supplicia sunt. Cum enim dicit: Tradidit illos deus, iam de uindicta est cuiusdam peccati, ut haec faciant. Qui commutauerunt ueritatem dei [258] in mendacium (ib., 25). Quid est, Commutauerunt ueritatem dei in mendacium? Pagan and Christian customs
Topic: Pagan customs and Christian customs. Location: Hippo. Date: New Year's Day.

1. As I see that today you have come as if it were a holiday and on the occasion of the date I find you gathered in greater numbers than usual, I urge your charity, brothers, to remember what you recently sang, lest, while the tongue cries out, the heart remains mute. Shout with affection before the ears of God the same thing that each of you pronounced orally before the ears of your neighbors. This is what you sang: Save us, Lord our God; Gather us from among the Gentiles to confess your name. And if the festival that the Gentiles celebrate today 1 in the midst of worldly and carnal joy, among the uproar of vain and extremely clumsy songs, in the no less clumsy banquets and dances, in the celebration of a festival that is no festival, if what the Gentiles do does not delight you, gather together from among the Gentiles. 2. You yourselves sang—and the sound of the divine song is still fresh in your ears—what follows: Save us, Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations.

useful. Who can be gathered from among the Gentiles unless he is saved? Therefore, those who mix with the Gentiles are not saved; On the other hand, those gathered from among the Gentiles are saved; saved with the salvation of faith, of hope, of the purest charity; with spiritual salvation, which is granted by the promises of God. Consequently, those who believe, hope and love should not automatically be declared saved. It is of great importance to know what you believe, what you hope for and what you love. In fact, no one, in any kind of life, lives without these three affections of the soul, that is, without believing, hoping and loving. If you do not believe what the Gentiles believe, nor hope what they hope for, nor love what they love, you are gathered from among the Gentiles, you are segregated or separated from them. And do not be afraid to find yourself mixed bodily, since the spiritual separation is so great. They believe that demons are gods, you believe in the one true God; They put their hope in worldly vanities, you in living eternally with Christ; They love the world, you love the creator of the world. Are there things more distant from each other than these? Whoever, therefore, believes, hopes and loves other things than theirs, prove it with life, demonstrate it with facts. If, like the pagan, you are going to exchange bouquets, participate in games of chance and get drunk, how come you believe, hope and love anything else? With what face do you sing: Save us, Lord our God, and congrévestris: Salva nos, Domine Deus noster, et congreganos de Gentibus. Quis potest congregan de Gentibus, nisi cum fit salvus? Qui ergo miscentur Gentibus, salvi non sunt; salvantur autem qui congregantur de Gentibus, salute fidei, salute spei, salute sincerissimae caritatis, salute spirituali, salute promissorum Dei. Qui ergo credit, sperat, et amat, non continuo salvus dicedus est. Interest enim quid credat, quid speret, et quid amet. Nemo quippe vivit in quacumque vita, sine tribus istis animae affectionibus, credendi, sperandi, amandi. Si non credis quod credunt Gentes, non speras quod [1025] sperant Gentes, non amas quod amant Gentes; you will congregate from Gentibus, you will segregate, hoc est you will separate from Gentibus. Nec terreat commixtio corporalis in tanta separatione mentís. The apostle Peter calls the Church, which is the body of Christ, a holy people, a royal priesthood. In fact, then only a single priest was anointed; Now all Christians are anointed. Both the king and the priest received the anointing, but no one else. The Lord was one thing and another, priest and king; not in figure, but in reality. For this reason the Apostle says, referring to the Lord himself: Who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. Here, then, is the royal lineage. It is said that Christ belongs to the line of David because of Mary, since she was of that line. But what lineage was Mary? In the gospel it is written that Zechariah, a priest, had as his wife Elizabeth, one of Aaron's daughters. Consequently, he belonged to the priestly lineage, as was the entire tribe of Levi. On the other hand, according to the gospel, the angel says to the virgin Mary: Your relative Elizabeth. We have seen his star in the east and we have come to worship him. They announce and ask, believe and search, as if symbolizing those who walk in faith and desire reality. Had not other kings of the Jews been born before in Judea? What does it mean that it is recognized by strangers in heaven and is sought on earth, that it shines on high and is hidden in lowliness? The wise men see the star in the east and understand that a king has been born in Judea. The same star took the wise men to the precise place where the Word God was, a speechless child. Let us now be ashamed of the sacrilegious foolishness and—worth the expression—a certain unlearned doctrine that judges that Christ was born under the influence of the stars, because it is written in the gospel that, when he was born, the wise men saw his star in the east. Which would not be true even if men were born under such influence, since they are not born, like the Son of God, of their own free will, but in the condition proper to mortal nature. Now, however, it is so far from the truth to say that Christ was born under the fate of the stars, that those who have right faith in Christ do not even believe that any man was born in that way. He punishes his servants when they sin in his house without first forcing himself to blaspheme against his gods, who radiate light from heaven. But as for Christ, not even conforming to their vain conjectures and their books, which I will call not fateful, but false, they cannot think that he was born under the law of the stars because, when he was born, the wise men saw a star in the east. Here Christ appears more as lord than as subject to it, since the star did not maintain its sidereal route in the sky, but rather showed the way to the place where he was born to the men who were looking for Christ. Consequently, it was not she who wonderfully made Christ live, but it was Christ who made her appear in an extraordinary way. Nor was she the one who decreed the wonderful actions of Christ, but Christ showed her among his wonderful works. He, born of a mother, from heaven showed the earth a new star; He who, born of the Father, made heaven and earth. When he was born a new light appeared with the star; When he died the ancient light was veiled by the sun. When he was born, the inhabitants of heaven shone with a new honor; When he died, the inhabitants of hell trembled with new fear. When he was resurrected, the disciples burned with new love, and when he ascended, the heavens opened with new submission. Let us therefore celebrate with devout solemnity also this day, on which the wise men, coming from the Gentiles, adored Christ once he was known, as we already celebrated that day on which the shepherds of Judea saw Christ once he was born. The same Lord and God our dam putet; quandoquidem ista sentendo servos suos in domo peccantes verberare non sinitur, nisi prius déos suos in cáelo radiantes blasphemare cogatur. Christum tamen isti nec secundum suas vanissimas coniecturas, et non sane fatídicos, sed plañe falsidicos libros, possunt ideo putare sub stellarum decree esse natum, quia eo nato stellam Magi in Oriente viderunt. Hinc enim potius Christus non sub dominatu eius, sed Dominus eius appatuit; quia iEa non in cáelo sidereas vias tenuit, sed hominibus quaerentibus Christum viam usque ad locum, in quo natus fuet, demonstravit. Ipse enim natus ex matre, de cáelo terrae novum sidus ostendit, qui natus ex Patre caelum terramque formavit. Eo nascente lux nova est in stella revelata, quo moriente lux antiqua est in sole velata. Eo nascente superi novo honore claruerunt, quo moriente inferí novo timote tremuerunt, quo resurgente discipuli novo amore exarserunt, quo ascending caeli new gift patuerunt. Celebremus ergo devota solemnitate et hunc diem, quo cognitum Christum Magi ex Gentibus adoraverunt (cf. Mt 2:1-11); sicut celebravimus illum diem, quo natum Christum pastores ex Judaea viderunt (cf. Lk 2:8-20). Ipse enim Dominus Deus noster elegit Apostólos

He chose the apostles from among the Jews as pastors to gather, through them, the sinners who were to be saved from the Gentiles.

sebre, and was already guiding the wise men from the east. Hidden in a stable, he was recognized in heaven, so that, recognized in heaven, he would manifest himself in the stable and this day would receive the name Epiphany, which can be translated as "manifestation." At the same time he shows his excellency and his humility, so that those who sought him would find him in a narrow stable that the open heavens showed with the signs of the stars; so that, although crippled by his childish limbs and wrapped in child's swaddling clothes, he would be adored by the wise men and feared by the wicked. 2. In fact, King Herod was filled with fear when the wise men came to him in search of the child, whose birth they had known from the testimony of heaven. What will his court be like when he acts as judge, if his crib as a child already terrified proud kings? How much more correct are the kings of today, who do not seek to kill him, like Herod, but rather delight in worshiping, like the wise men, whom he suffered for his enemies, at the hand of his own enemies, the same death that his enemy wanted to cause him, and with his death he put death to death in his body! Let the kings now feel a pious fear of him who is already seated at the right hand of the Father; whom he already feared, when he was still taking his mother's breast, that impious king. Listen to what is written: And now, kings, understand; Instruct you who judge the earth: serve the Lord with fear and exult before him with trembling. That king, in fact, avenger of wicked kings and guide of the pious, was not born like the kings in this world, since the one who was born is the king whose kingdom is not of this world. Topic: The manifestation of the Lord. Location: Hippo. Date: Epiphany Day (January 6). Before 405.

1. The wise men came from the east to worship the birth of the Virgin. We celebrate this date today by granting it the well-deserved solemnity and sermon. This day shone for them for the first time; for us it returns annually on this holiday. They were the firstfruits of the Gentiles, we are the Gentile people. The language of the apostles announced it to us; to them, a star, like the language of the heavens; The apostles themselves, as if they were heavens, proclaimed to us the glory of God. How can we not recognize that those that have become thrones of God are heavens? Thus it is written: The soul of the righteous is the throne of wisdom. Through these heavens thundered the maker and dweller of the heavens; thunder that scared the world, and behold, it now believes. Great mystery! He still lay in the peex Iudaea pastores, per quos congregaret salvandos etiam ex Gentibus peccatores. SERMO
IN EPIPHANIA DOMINI,

CAPUT I.—1. Manifestationis Christi solemnitas.—Ad partum Virginis adorandum Magi ab Oriente venerunt. Hunc diem hodie celebramus, huic debitam solemnitatem sermonemque persolvimus. lilis dies iste primus illuxit, anniversaria nobis festivitate rediit. lili weret primitiae Gentium, nos populus Gentium. Nobis hoc lingua nuntiavit Apostolorum, stella illis tanquam lingua caelorum; et nobis idem Apostolic, tanquam caeli, enarraverunt gloriam Dei [1029] (cf. Ps 18,1). Cur enim non agnoscamus eos cáelos, qui facti sunt sedes Dei? sicut scriptum est: Anima iusti, sedes est sapientiae (cf. Sap 7). Per hos enim cáelos ille caelorum fabricator et habitator intonuit, quo tonitru mundus contremuit, et ecce iam credit. Magnum sacramentum. In praesepi tune iacebat, et Magos ab Oriente ducebat. Abscondebatur in stabulo, et agnoscebatur in cáelo; ut agnitus in cáelo manifestetur in stabulo, et appellaretur

Epiphania dies iste, quod latine manifestatio dici potest: simul eius celsitudinem humilitatenique commendans, ut qui in aperto cáelo signis sidereis monstrabatur, in angustodiverso quaesitus inveniretur; invalidus infantilibus membris, involutus infantilibus pannis, adoraretur a Magis, timeretur a malis. 2. Herodis terror.—Timuit enim eum rex Herod, eisdem sibi Magis nuntiantibus, cum adhuc quaererent parvulum, quem cognoverant cáelo teste iam natum. Quid erit tribunal iudicantis, quando superbos reges crinae terrebant infantis? Quanto consultius nunc reges, non sicut Herodes, interficere quaerunt; sed sicut Magi potius, adorare delectantur, iam praesertim eum qui et ipsam mortem quam cupiebat inimicus inferre, etiam pro ipsis inimicis ab inimicis sustinuit, eamque in suo corpore occisus occidit. Pie timeant nunc reges ad Patris dexteram iam sedentem, quem rex ille impius timuit adhuc matris ubera lambentem. Audiant quod scriptum est: Et nunc, reges, intelligite; erudimini, qui iudicatis terram: serve Domino in timore, et exsultate ei cum tremore (Ps 2,1011). Ille enim rex, ultor impiorum regum, et rector piorum, non ita natus est, ut reges nascuntur in saeculo; quia et ille natus est, cuius regnum
The manifestation of the Lord

manifested in the virginity of the mother, and the nobility of the mother, in the divinity of the born. Finally, although there had been many kings of the Jews born and dead, none of them ever asked magi to worship him, because they did not know any of them by the voice of heaven. 3. But, and the fact must not be overlooked, this illumination of the wise men was the great testimony of the blindness of the Jews. The former were searching in their land for someone they did not recognize in their own. Among them they found, speechless, the one whom the Jews denied when he taught. These pilgrims who came from afar worshiped Christ, a child who did not yet speak, where the citizens crucified him when, already mature, he worked miracles. The wise men recognized him as God in the smallness of his members; The Jews did not even forgive him as a man when he did great deeds. As if it were a greater thing to see a shining new star on the day of its birth than to see the sun cry on the day of its death! But that same star that led the wise men to the place where the child God was with his virgin mother and that could certainly have guided them to the city itself, was hidden and did not appear to them again until they had asked the Jews about the city in which Christ was to be born, so that they would name it according to the testimony of the Holy Scripture and say: "In Bethlehem of Judah." Thus it is written: "And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are not the least among the

princes of Judah, for from you will come the leader who will rule my people Israel. What else did divine Providence mean by this but that the only divine writings with which the Gentiles were to be instructed and they were to be blinded would remain in the possession of the Jews; that they would carry them not as support for their salvation, but as a testimony of ours? Well today, when we preserve the ancient prophecies about Christ, already clarified in the light of the events that have occurred, if by chance the pagans whom we want to win were to tell us that these things were not predicted beforehand, but after what had been announced, so that what is thought to be a prophecy was an invention of the Christians, we turn to the codices of the Jews to overcome the doubt of the pagans. Pagans who were already figured in those magicians whom the Jews instructed with the divine Scriptures about the city in which Christ was born, whom they neither sought nor recognized.

It is not de hoc saeculo. Nobilitas fuet nascentis, in virginitate paríentis; et nobilitas parientis, in divinitate nascentis. Denique cum tam multi iam nati atque defuncti essent reges ludaeorum, nunquam quemquam eorum adorandum Magi quaesierunt; quia nec quemquam eorum cáelo loquente didicerunt. CAPUT II.—3. ludaeorum caecitas in ipsa illuminatione Magorum. Scripturae apud ludaeos propter Gentium fidem relictae.—Verumtamen, quod praetereundum non est, haec Magorum illuminatio magnum testimonium caecitatis exstitit ludaeorum. In terra eorum isti requirebant, quem illi in sua non agnoscebant. Apud eos isti infantem invenerunt, quem illi apud se maestrom negaverunt. In his terris de longinquo isti peregrini puerum Christum nondum verba promentem adoraverunt, ubi cives illi iuvenem miracula facientem crucifixerunt. Isti in membris parvis Deum agnoverunt; illi in factis magnis nec tanquam homini pepercerunt: quasi plus fuerit videre novam stellam in [1030] eius nativitate fulgentem, quam solem eius in morte lugentem. Iam vero quod eadem stella, quae Magi perduxit ad locum ubi erat cum matre virgine Deus infans, quae utique poterat eos et ad ipsam perducere civitatem, se tamen subtraxit, nec eis prorsus apparuit, doñee de civitate, in qua Christus nasceretur, iidem ipsi interrogarentur Iudaei, ut ipsi eam secundum divinae Scripturae testimonium nominarent, ipsi dicerent: In Bethlehem Iudae. Sic enim scriptum est: Et tu Bethlehem, terra luda, non es minima

4. Now therefore, dearly beloved, children and heirs of grace, consider your vocation and, once Christ has been revealed to the Jews and the Gentiles, cling to him with untiring love as to a cornerstone. Indeed, at the beginning of his inin principibus Tuda: ex te enin exiet dux qui reget populum meum Israel (Mt 2,5-6): quid aliud hic significavit divina providentia, nisi apud ludaeos solas divinas Litteras remansuras, quibus Gentes instruerentur, illi excaecarentur; quas portarent non ad adiutorium salutis suae, sed ad testimonium salutis nostrae? Nam hodie cum praemissas prophetias de Christo proferimus, iam rerum completionum luz declaratas, si forte Pagani, quos lucrari volumus, dixerint non eas mucho ante praedictas, sed post rerum eventum, ut haec quae facta sunt prophetata putarentur, a nobis esse confictas; ludaeorum codices recitamus, ut tollatur dubitatio Paganorum: qui iam in Magis illis figurabantur, quos Iudaei de civitate in qua natus est Christus, divinis eloquiis instruebant, et eum ipsi nec requirebant, nec agnoscebant. CAPUT III.—4. Christo caritate cum Iudaeis Gentes cohaerent.— Nunc ergo, carissimi, gratiae filii et heredes, videte vocationem vestram, et manifestato Iudaeis et Gentibus Christo tanquam angulari lapidi perseverantissima dilectione cohaerete. Manifestatus enim est in ipsis cenabulis infantiae suae his qui prope, et his qui longe erant; Iudaeis In its apologetic work, ancient Christianity used anti-testamentary prophecies more than the miracles of Jesus. This caused the pagans to react by denying the reality of the prophecies themselves; According to them, they were inventions of Christians, ex eventu predictions, like those of Virgil (Aeneid VI 752-887), according to Augustine himself (serm.374,2). The accusation appears repeatedly in the Augustinian pages. See sermons 201,3; 373.4; 374.2; Treatises on the gospel of Saint John 35,7; Comments on Psalms 40:14; 56.9. In all these texts he also speaks of the service provided in this regard by the Jews, who by preserving the Scriptures attested to the authenticity of the prophecies. Their testimony was of great value, because they were declared enemies of the Christian name. In other texts he alludes to prophecies outside of Christianity; specifically, of Sibyl (The City of God XVIII 46; The Concordance of the Evangelists I 20,28).

fancy was manifested both to those who were near and to those who were far away. To the Jews, in the proximity of the shepherds, and to the Gentiles, in the distance of the wise men. Topic: The manifestation of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Epiphany Day (January 6). 1. A few days ago we celebrated the birth of the Lord; Today, however, we celebrate, with solemnity no less deserved, its first manifestation to the Gentiles. On that day the Jewish shepherds saw him newborn; Today the wise men from the East worshiped him. In effect, that cornerstone had been born in which the wall of circumcision and that of the foreskin found peace, whose diversity of origin was not exactly small; It was born so that they could be united in it, which became our peace and made the two peoples one. This was symbolized in the persons of the shepherds of Israel and in the wise men of the east. Then began what was going to grow and bear fruit throughout the world. We, therefore, consider these two days, that of the birth and that of the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ, as pleasant dates, per superbiam fracti haeretici sunt facti, quoniam potens est Deus iterum inserere illos (cf. Rom 11,17-24), habeamus infatigabilem caritatem. SERMO
IN EPIPHANIA DOMINI,

CAPUT I.—1. Manifested Christi facta Gentibus. Stella lingua caeli. Ante paucissimos dies Natalem Domini celebravimus: hodierno autem die manifestationem, qua manifesti Gentibus coepit, solemnitate non minus debita celebramus. Illo die natum shepherds Iudaei viderunt: hodie Magi ab Oriente venientes adoraverunt. Natus quippe fuet lapis ille angularis, pax duorum parietum et circumcisione et praeputio, non ex parva diversitate venientium; ut in illo copularentur, qui factus est pax nostra, et fecit utraque unum (cf. Eph 2,11-22). Hoc in pastoribus Iudaeorum, et Magis Gentium praesignatum est. Inde coepit, quod in universe world fructificadoret et cresceret. Nos itaque duos dies, Nativitatis et Manifestationis Domini nostri, spirituali laetitia gratissimos 2 The Donatists,

chasms and full of spiritual joy. The Jews were led to him by the angel's announcement; the wise men, by the indication of a star. This star confuses the vain calculations and riddles of astrologers, since it showed the worshipers of the stars that the one who should be worshiped was the creator of heaven and earth. In fact, he who when he died darkened the old sun, he himself manifested the new star at birth. That light began the faith of the Gentiles, that darkness was an accusation against the perfidy of the Jews. What star was that which had never appeared before among the stars nor remained afterwards so that we could see it? What else was it but the extraordinary language of heaven that appeared to narrate the glory of God and proclaim with its unusual brilliance the unusual birth of a virgin, who was to succeed, once she disappeared, the Gospel throughout the entire globe of the earth? Finally, what did the wise men say when they arrived? Where is the born king of the Jews? What does this mean? Had not numerous kings of the Jews been born before? Why so much effort to know and worship the king of a strange people? We have seen, they said, his star in the east, and we have come to worship him. Would they seek him with such devotion, would they desire him with such pious affection, if they had not recognized in the king of the Jews the one who is also king of the ages? 2. Hence Pilate was also inspired by an aura of truth when in the passion he ordered the title King of the Jews to be written; title that the Jews, liars, wanted to correct, habeamus. Iudaei pastors ad eum angelo nuntiante, gentiles Magi stella demonstrante perducti sunt. Haec stella vanas computationes astrologorum divinationesque confudit, cum stellarum adoratoribus Creatorem caeli et terrae adorandum potius demonstravit. Nam ipse novam stellam declaravit natus, qui antiquum solem obscuravit occisus. Illa luz inchoata est fides Gentium; illis tenebris accusata est perfidia Iudaeorum. Quid erat illa stella, quae nec unquam antea Inter sidera apparuit, nec postea demonstranda permansit? Quid erat, nisi magnifica lingua caeli, quae narraret gloriam Dei, quae inusitatum virginís partum inusitato fulgore clamaret, cui postea non apparenti Evangelium toto orbe succederet? Quid denique Magi venientes dixerunt? Ubi est qui natus est rex Iudaeorum? Quid est hoc? Nonne tam multi antea reges erant nati Iudaeorum?

Quid bothpere alienae gentis regem nosse et adorare cupiérunt? Vidimus enim, inquiunt, stellam eius in Oriente, et venimus adorare eum (Mt 2,2). Numquid hoc tanta devotione requirerent, tan pietatis affectu desiderarent, nisi eum agnoscerent regem Iudaeorum, qui rex est etiam saeculorum? CAPOT II.—2.. In Pilato et Magis significatae Gentes ab Oriente et Occident congregandae.—Hinc et Pilatus nonnulla utique aura veritatis afflatus est, quando in eius passione titulum scripsit: Rex Iudaeorum; quem Iudaei conati sunt mendosi emendare. Quibus Ule responded:
The manifestation of the Lord

and to whom he answered: What I have written, I have written, for we find in the psalm: Do not change the inscription of the title. Let us consider this great and wonderful mystery. Both the wise men and Pilate were Gentiles; The first saw the star in the sky, the second wrote the title on the tree, but all were looking for or recognized not the king of the Gentiles, but the king of the Jews. The Jews, on the other hand, neither saw the star nor agreed with the title. It was already symbolized there what the Lord later said: Many will come from the east and the west and will sit in the kingdom of heaven at the table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; Instead, the children of the kingdom will go to the outer darkness. In fact, the wise men had come from the east, and Pilate from the west; hence they bear witness to him as king of the Jews when he is born (east) and he when he dies (west) to sit in the kingdom of heaven at the table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from whom the Jews originated. They did not come from these by the flesh, but had been grafted into them by faith, already anticipating the wild olive tree that was to be grafted into the olive tree of which the Apostle speaks. This, then, is the reason why the Gentiles themselves did not seek or recognize in him the king of the Gentiles, but rather the king of the Jews: because it was the wild olive tree that came to the olive tree, not the olive tree to the wild olive tree. However, the branches that were to be pruned, that is, the unbelieving Jews, at the same time that they responded that in Bethlehem of Judah to the wise men who asked where Christ was to be born, obstinately showed themselves Quod scripsí, scripsi (lo 19,19.22); quía praedictum erat in Psalm: Tituli inscriptionem ne corrumpas (Ps 56,1). Advertamus itaque magnum hoc et mirabile sacramentum. Magi ex [1032] Gentibus erant, ipse etiam Pilatus ex Gentibus: illi stellam viderunt in cáelo, tile titulum scripsit in ligno: utrique tamen non regem Gentium, sed Iudaeorum vel quaerebant, vel agnoscebant. Iudaei vero ipsi nec stellam secuti sunt, nec titulo consenserunt. Iam igitur praesignabatur quod postea ipse Dominus dixit: Multi ab Oriente et Occident venient, et recumbent cum Abraham et Isaac et Iacob in regno caelorum: filii autem regni ibunt in exterior tenebras (Mt 8,11-12). Nam Magi ab Oriente, Pilatus ab Occident venerat.

Uhde illi orienti, hoc est nascenti; ille autem occidenti, hoc est mororienti, attestabantur regi Iudaeorum: ut cum Abraham et Isaac et Iacob, ex quibus Iudaei ducebant originem, recumberent in regno caelorum; non ex eis propagad per carnem, sed eis inserti per fidem: ut ille de quo Apostolus loquitur, olivae inserendus iam praemonstraretur oleaster (cf. Rom 11:24). Propterea quippe non rex Gentium, sed Iudaeorum ab eisdem Gentibus, vel quaerebatur, vel agnoscebatur; quia oleaster ad olivam, non ad oleastrum oliva veniebat. Rami tamen frangendi, hoc est, infideles Iudaei, et Magis inquirentibus ubi Christus nasceretur, In Bethlehem ludae, responderbant (Mt_2,5); et Pilate exprobrante quod regem suum crucifigi vellent, pertinacissime

cruel before Pilate, who reproached them for wanting to crucify their king. In this way, the wise men worshiped him after the Jews had shown them the place of Christ's birth: it is in the Scripture, given to the Jews, where we recognize Christ. Pi] a. He, a Gentile, washed his hands when the Jews asked him for the death of Christ: the blood that the Jews shed is what washes away our sins. Of the testimony that Pilate gave, through the title in which he wrote that Christ was the king of the Jews, there is another occasion to speak: the time of the passion. 3. Now let us say how little remains to us regarding the manifestation of Christ after his birth, from the day of that manifestation, which in the Greek language is called Epiphany, the day on which he began to manifest himself to the Gentiles in the persons of the wise men who worshiped him. It is more and more delighting to consider how the Jews responded to the wise men, who asked them where Christ was to be born, that in Bethlehem of Judah, and yet, they did not accompany them, but it was the same star that, when it set out, led them to the place where the little one was. In this way it was clear that it could also show the city, but that it had been removed from view for a short time so that the Jews could be interrogated. And the Jews were questioned to demonstrate that they were bearers of divine testimony not for their personal salvation and knowledge, but for the Gentiles. The Jewish people were expelled from their kingdom and dispersed throughout the land for this purpose: so that they would be

everywhere forced witnesses of faith in the one whose enemies they were. In fact, having lost the temple, the sacrifices, the priesthood and the kingdom itself, they preserve their name and their race, united to a few ancient rites, lest, mixed indiscriminately with the Gentiles, they disappear and cease to be a testimony in favor of the truth. In the same way, Cain received a sign so that no one would kill the one who killed his brother out of envy and pride. Without a doubt, this can also be understood, without violating the text, in Psalm 58, in which Christ, speaking in place of his body, says: My God showed himself to me in my enemies; do not put them to death, lest they ever forget your law. In fact, through these enemies of the faith it is demonstrated to the Gentiles that Christ was prophesied; It could happen that, upon seeing such clarity in the fulfillment of the prophecies, they might come to think that the Scriptures themselves had been invented by Christians 2, since they read what they saw had been fulfilled as prophesied by Christ. The Jews provide the codices, and in this way God manifests himself to us in our enemies. He did not kill them, that is, he has not completely exterminated them from the face of the earth, so that they do not forget his law. When they read it and fulfill some of its precepts, even carnally, they remember it for their own condemnation and give us a testimony in our favor.

Pilatus ex Gentibus manus lavit, Iudaeis mortem Christi petentibus (cf. ib., 27,24); quia sanguine quem Iudaei fuderunt, nostra peccata diluimus. Thirst for testimony Pilati per titulum, in quo scripsit regem Iudaeorum esse Christum, alius est disserendi locus: quo passionis est tempus. CAPUT III.—3. The manifestation of the Lord

Topic: The manifestation of the Lord. Location: Unknown. Date: Epiphany Day (January 6). Previous to 411. 1. The date invites us to speak to you, like every year, about today's solemnity, known throughout the world; of what is festive for us and what we commemorate in this annual celebration. Epiphany is a Greek term that we can translate as "manifestation." We are told that on this day the wise men worshiped the Lord, warned by the appearance of a star that went ahead guiding them. On the same day that he was born they saw the star in the east, and they recognized who was the one whose birth had been indicated to them. From that very day until today they were on the road, they terrified King Herod with their proclamation and they met the Jews, who, with the prophetic Scripture in their hands, answered them that Bethlehem was the city in which the Lord was to be born. Having the same star as their guide, they then came to the Lord himself, and, when he was shown to them, they worshiped him, offered him gold, frankincense and myrrh, and returned by another way. On the same day of his birth he appeared to some shepherds warned by the angels, and on the same day, far away in the east, the wise men received the announcement through a star, but only on this date was he worshiped by them. The entire Church of the Gentiles has agreed to celebrate this day with the utmost devotion, for what else were those wise men but the firstfruits of the Gentiles? The shepherds were Israelites; the wise men, Gentiles; those came from close by; these, from afar; but both agreed on the cornerstone. The Apostle says: When he came, he announced peace to us who were far away and to those who were near. Indeed, he is our peace, who made both peoples one, and formed them both into one new man, establishing peace, and transformed them both into one body for God, putting to death in himself the enmities. 2. On that day, in fact, the child, before he knew how to call his father or his mother, as had been prophesied of him, received the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria; That is to say, before he uttered human words through human flesh, he received the power of Damascus, that is, the power that Damascus boasted. That city, once flourishing by the world's standards, had boasted of its riches. Among these, the first place is reserved for gold, precisely what the wise men humbly offer to Christ. The spoils of Samaria, in turn, were its own inhabitants. eis est adoratus. The manifestation of the Lord

Samaria, in fact, is placed in the place of idolatry, because there, after having separated from God, the people of Israel converted to the worship of idols. Coming to destroy the kingdom of the devil throughout the world with the spiritual sword, Christ, while still a child, snatched these first spoils from the domination of idolatry. He removed from the pestilence of such superstition the magicians who had set out to worship him, and, not yet able to speak on earth with the tongue, he spoke from heaven through the star, and showed, not with the voice of the flesh, but with the power of the Word, who he was, whence, and by whom he had come. This Word, which in the beginning was God within God, already made flesh to dwell among us, had come to us and remained with the Father; Without abandoning the angels above, through them he gathers men to himself here below. He shines with unchangeable truth before the inhabitants of heaven as a Word and lies in a manger because of the smallness of the inn. He made a star appear in the sky that indicated him on earth as worthy of worship. And, despite being such a powerful, great child, while still small, carried by his parents, he fled to Egypt due to Herod's hostility; In this way he spoke, although not with words, but with actions, and in silence he said: If they persecute you in one city, flee to another2. He carried human flesh, in which he foreshadowed us and in which he was to die for us at the opportune moment.

This was the reason why the wise men offered him not only gold and incense, as a sign of honor and adoration, respectively, but also myrrh, as he was to be buried. In the children whom Herod killed, he showed how those who died for him would be, how innocent and how humble. In his two years of age he also signified the number of the precepts on which all the law and the prophets hang. 3. Who is not surprised that the Jews responded according to Scripture to the question of the wise men about where Christ was to be born and did not go to worship him with them? What does this mean? When they kill the lamb and eat the Passover, do they not proclaim Christ to the Gentiles, without worshiping Him? What else does our action express regarding the testimonies of the prophets, in which Christ is pre-announced? To the men who suspect that such testimonies were written by Christians 3, not when they were still future, but after the events had occurred, we place them before the codices of the Jews to confirm their doubtful intentions.
