The event took place tonight. There is no doubt that the days begin to be counted from the preceding night, although it does not conform to the order of days mentioned in Genesis, although there also the darkness has preceded the day, since the darkness was hanging over the abyss when God said: "Let there be light, and there was light." But since that darkness was not yet night, there were no days either. In fact, God made the division between light and darkness, and first called the light day, and then the darkness night, and the space from the moment the light became until the next morning was mentioned as one day. It is clear that those days began with the light, and, after the night, each lasted until the next morning. But after man created by the light of justice fell into the darkness of sin, from which the grace of Christ freed him, it has come to pass that we count the days from the nights, because our effort is not directed toward passing from light to darkness, but from darkness to light, which we hope to achieve with the help of the Lord. Thus also says the Apostle: The night is past, the day is at hand; Let us, therefore, put off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light. Therefore, the day of the Lord's passion, the day on which he was crucified, followed the night itself, already past, and that is why it closed and concluded in the preparation of the Passover, which the Jews also call "pure supper," and the observance of the Sabbath began at the beginning of this night. Topic: Be alert against the devil. Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Vigil.

Although the very solemnity of this holy night already exhorts you, dearly beloved, to watch and pray, it is my duty to address you a few words so that the voice of the shepherd may also put the flock of the Lord on alert against those who oppose and envy him: the powers and rulers of this darkness, as if against nocturnal beasts. As the Apostle says: Our struggle is not against flesh or blood, that is, against men weak because of the mortality of their body, but against the princes, the powers and the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the evil spirits of the air. And do not think that the Apostle with these words is indicating that the devil and his angels are the rulers of this world, of which it is written: And the world was made by him. For, having mentioned the rulers of the world, so that no one would understand under the word "world" what in numerous places in Scripture is designated by the name of "heaven" and "earth," he then added, as if to clarify it: of this darkness, that is, of the infidels. Praise what he did and praise him who did it. In the beginning God made heaven and earth. Behold, what is done is before the eyes, it is seen, it pleases. The work is patent, the craftsman is latent, since what allows us to see is also revealed, and what allows us to love is hidden. When we see the world and love God, what allows us to love is, without a doubt, better than what seeing gives us. We see with our eyes and we love with our heart 2. Let us, then, put the heart before the eyes, also because he whom we love, without seeing him, is better than his work, which we have in sight. Let us investigate, then, if you please, when God made this mass and what means he used. The instrument of the craftsman was his word. What do you miss? It is the work of the almighty 3. If you want to know who made it, God made it; If you want to know what he made, he made heaven and earth; If you want to know by what he made them, he made them by the Word, which he did not make. The Word, by which heaven and earth were made, was not made. Indeed, if it was made, by whom was it made? Everything was done by her. If everything that has been made has been done by the Word, without a doubt the Word, by which everything was made, has not been made. Thus, the servant of God Moses, narrator of the creation, said: In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. He made heaven and earth in the beginning. By what means did he do it? Through the Word. Did he also make the Word? No; what to say then? In the beginning there was the Word. The Word already existed, by which he did everything; So he made what did not exist. The Word can also be considered the principle in which God made heaven and earth. The same Word, in fact, is also the wisdom of God, to whom it is said: You did everything in wisdom. If God made everything in wisdom, and, without a doubt, the only begotten Son is the wisdom of God, we must not doubt that everything we have learned was done through him was done in the Son. Indeed, the Son is the Beginning. When the Jews asked him, "Who are you?", he answered them, "The Beginning." Behold, in the beginning God made heaven and earth. Better absolutely is God. Why do you look for the best in the inferior? In your being, the body is inferior to the mind; In the totality of things, there is nothing better than God. Elevate what is most excellent in you, to reach, if you can, the one who is better than everything. I too, when I speak, address minds. I too, who am visible in the body, see the visible faces; but, using what I see, I address what I do not see. I carry inside the word conceived in my heart, and I want to illuminate in your ears what I have conceived in my heart; I want to tell you what is inside, communicate to you what is hidden; I'm looking for a way to reach your mind. But Moses was a man and his being was not such in comparison with that of God; It existed on earth, it existed in the flesh; The soul resided in the flesh itself, was mutable by nature and was under the weight of human frailty. When was he going to understand those words: I am who I am? Behold, using what his eyes saw, he spoke to those who did not see, and God, hidden, used as an instrument what Moses saw. In fact, what Moses saw was not God in his entirety, nor is it the entirety of my word for me to say that I am a man. I have a word in my mind that doesn't sound; The sound passes, the word remains. Therefore, when God said to man, that is, when the invisible spoke in a sensible way through that whose form he deigned to take; when the eternal spoke temporary things or the immutable things expired; when God said: I am that I am and You will say to the children of Israel: "He who is sent me to you," as if Moses could not understand what these words mean: I am who I am and He who is sent me to you, or perhaps, although he could understand it, but not we who would read it later, after having indicated the name of his being, he added the name of his mercy. For Christ died once, the just for the unjust; but, once resurrected from the dead, he dies no more and death has no dominion over him. In fact, as soon as he died to sin, he died only once; On the other hand, as long as he lives, he lives for God. So let us also judge ourselves to be dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus. In order for the memory to always preserve this sublime mystery, it was appropriate that the day on which such an event took place should be distinguished from the other nights, and, thanks to this well-known solemnity, it should be made present to the hearts of pious men. The Jews killed Christ to erase his memory from the earth. But, except for eternal punishment, they have only managed to ensure that the world does not forget either their memory, already famous, or their own crime. Everyone who on earth admires the light of this night, at the same time detests the darkness of the Jews. Let us also abhor his crime; Let us keep only the good that the Lord extracted from his evil and let us celebrate it with all solemnity.

Theme: Easter is the fight between two lions. Location: Hippo. Date: Easter night. 1. We celebrate in this vigil, dear brothers, the annual solemnity of that night when Jesus Christ the Lord rose from the dead. I am not trying to teach it to you now, but, since you already know it, I urge you not to forget it. And as the festival itself with its solemn return on the appropriate date does not teach us anything new, but prevents forgetting from erasing what we already know - since it renews the memory, without adding any knowledge -, in the same way, my words, although they are not addressed to ignorant people, nevertheless require your attention, since I do not intend for you to hear something that is unknown to you, but I do want you to remember with joy what you know. 2. Qui saevituris et mororienti insultaturis inimicis in prophetia dixit: numquid, qui dormit, non adiciet ut resurgat? (Ps 40,9) Ergo, qui dormivit, etiam evigilavit, et sibi evigilanti
good and bad vigils

He consecrated this our vigil to himself. Let us therefore keep watch and pray, so as not to fall into temptation, because he also kept watch and became like a solitary bird on the roof; That is why he resurrected and flew to the heights and is the only one who intercedes for us in heaven. Let us present our prayers to such a great intercessor; He grants, together with the Father, what he asked of the Father, since he is mediator and creator; mediator to ask, creator to grant; mediator made in the world, creator by whom the world was made. Let us watch over him with a sober mind and with affection full of faith and trust, and let us present to him the prayer that he taught us, so that we can do with his help what he commanded us to do, and receive, by giving it to us, what he promised we would receive.

To celebrate in our vigil his awakening from the dead, can the members who have yet to sleep do anything more appropriate than to imitate, while the time comes, his head, now awakened forever, keeping vigil too, since they must do so like him and must reign with him in an eternal vigil, in which there will be no sleep? Precisely, then, every so often this great festival tells us what eternity will be like, where time will have no end. Let us, therefore, watch over Christ awake, and, as we can, deprive ourselves of sleep for a little while in honor of him who is no longer dominated by sleep. Keeping ourselves on his guard, let us be the true Israel according to the spirit: The guardian of Israel will not sleep or slumber. Watching in this annual solemnity for the guardian who no longer sleeps, let us tie our hearts to his hand, through the bond of faith, so that he does not depart, held by that bond, from those who are unaware of sleep until, mortality and corruption having disappeared, we completely unite ourselves with his organism, where we too will never again be able to sleep or doze. 2. This is the result of our vigils, this is the purpose to which the eyes look; not those of the flesh, but those of the spirit: the righteous and holy purpose of mastering and repressing sleep; and this is the incorruptible reward for the fatigue suffered and the love enkindled: that the one for whom we are awake, resisting earthly sleep for a short time, grants us life where there is wakefulness without fatigue, day without night and rest without sleep. Being awake is not worthy of praise.

But let us now also talk about those who do it for innocent purposes: watch the craftsmen, the farmers, the sailors, the fishermen, the travelers, the merchants, the administrators of anything, the judges, the lawyers, the buyers and sellers of books, those invested with power, their subjects and, finally, all those who are related to the arts or the industry with which human life is concerned; but with the aim of making the permanence on this land more bearable and more dignified for its inhabitants, who must pass through it with the speed of an exhalation. We are celebrating the solemn feast of the humility of the Lord, who humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. That is the reason why we humble our souls tonight through fasting, vigil and prayer, without the present fervor detracting from that humility. What, in fact, is the mustard seed but the fervor of humility? By means of this grain the mountains have been transferred to the heart of the sea; that is, the great preachers of the Gospel, the holy apostles were translated from Judea to the land of the Gentiles; and even of the heart of the world, that is, of the thoughts of the world, the mountains became masters of whom it was said: Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; and also: You shine wonderfully from the eternal mountains. Those same illuminated mountains, scorched at their summits, transferred themselves to the heart of the sea, that is, to the faith of the Gentiles, and they also took with them the light that illuminates every man, like a mountain of mountains, king of kings and saint of saints, so that what was predicted by the prophet would be fulfilled in them: In the last days it will be SERMO

our God: Enlighten my eyes so that I may never fall asleep in death, lest my enemy say, "I have prevailed over him." This enemy is the one who has manipulated the foolish Jews, as if they were his own instruments and weapons, against our Lord Jesus Christ; but he did not prevail against him. The enemies of the flesh believed they had prevailed, but the spiritual enemy was defeated in them. The impure spirit was defeated with a victim of pure flesh, and in the very act of inflaming men to do publicly what they wanted, he secretly suffered what he did not want, because by putting Christ to death he shed the blood through which those whom he killed would be revived. But he can't even count him among the dead. He was pained, in fact, to see those he wanted to associate with his death associated with the resurrection of Christ. In this life we ​​celebrate the death of the one whose life we ​​hope for after this death. So let us remember the humility of our Lord Jesus Christ through our own humility. Let us humbly watch, humbly pray, with most devout faith, most firm hope and most ardent charity, thinking of the day that will possess our clarity if our humility turns night into day. The Apostle exhorted us to pray, and at the same time to be vigilant, with these words: Apply yourselves to prayer, being vigilant in it. Impure love, brothers, forces those it dominates to remain awake. The impudent man watches to destroy virginity; the evil one, to do harm; the drunk, to drink; the robber, to kill; the prodigal, to waste; the miser, to store; the thief, to steal, and the pirate, to capture. How much more reason should charity guard the saints and innocents, if evil forces the clumsy and criminals to do so! But they are oppressed by a sleep of the heart so deep that it forces them to be awake in the flesh. Against that dream one gratia dei nobiscum, cuius promissum habemus, dicente propheta: educet sicut lumen iustitiam tuam (Ps 36,6). Beatus apostolus Paulus, omnes, inquit, vos filii lucís estis et filii diei: non sumus noctis ñeque tenebrarum. Itaque non dormiamus sicut et ceteri, sed vigilemus et sobrii simus. Nam qui dormiunt nocte dormiunt, et qui inebriantur nocte ebrii sunt. We autem qui diei sumus, sobrii

they get drunk. But we who are of the day are sober. What is this night, brothers, in which the Truth does not want us to meet and in which it says that those who sleep are found? And what is that dream that separates us children from light and day and in which it exhorts us not to fall asleep? Without a doubt, it is not the night that begins with the setting of the sun and ends with the brightness of the dawn, but rather another that begins with the fall of man and ends with the renewal of the soul. On this night even those who are awake are asleep, but they are bad, and those who, although they sleep, are good are not found. When this ordinary night comes, the day ends; That guilty night deprived us of that day that made this day. This dream that we resist with our vigilance receives a non-guilty death when the senses become numb; but that other dream in which the hearts of the unbelievers sleep pushes death to the inner eyes. Against him let us hear: Watch and pray; Against this let us say: Enlighten my eyes so that I never fall asleep in death. Having these torches, let us therefore keep a solemn vigil during this night in fight against bodily sleep; On the other hand, against the sleep of the heart we must ourselves be burning torches in this world, as if we were in the night. sumus (1 Thess 5,5-8). Qualis est ista nox, fratres, in qua nos esse veritas non vult, in qua dicit eos esse qui dormiunt? [742] Et qualis somnus est iste, a quo nos filios lucis dieique discernit, et quo somno ne dormiamus alloquitur? Procul dubio non est ista nox cuius initium est solis occasus, sed hominis casus, nec cui finem facit aurorae rutilatio, (719) sed animae renovatio. In the night you sleep there are vigilantes mali; in hac night non sunt etiam dormientes boni. Nox ista vulgarís coming terminat diem; nox illa damnabilis ab illo die nos abstulit qui fecit hunc diem. Somnus iste, cui moda resistimus vigilantes, inculpabilem sopientibus sensibus accipit mortem; somnus iüe, quo in corde dormiunt infideles, interior oculos urguet in mortem. Contra istum audiamus: invigilate et orate; contra illum dicamus: illumina oculos meos, ne umquam obdormiam in mortem. Solemniter itaque contra corporis somnum habentes ista in hac nocte luminaria vigilemus; contra illum vero somnum cordis tanquam in nocte in hoc saeculo nos ipsi luminaria esse debenmus.

Today, once the solemnity of the mysteries has been celebrated, those baptized and regenerated in Christ will intermingle with all the people of God. We are going to address them to them: to you in them and to them in you. See that you have become members of Christ. If you consider what you have become, all your bones will say: "Lord, who is like you?" Indeed, divine condescension can never be considered as it deserves; Don't words and senses fail us in the face of the fact that free grace has come to us without any precedent merit? That is why it is called grace: because it has been freely given to us. What grace am I talking about? Of the grace of being members of Christ and children of God; that you too are brothers of the only Son. If he is the only Son, how are you brothers except because he is the only Son by nature and you are his brothers by grace? Since you are members of Christ, here is my exhortation. Listen to me, those with whom you are going to mix. Today I fear for you, not so much because of the pagans, nor the Jews, nor the heretics, but because of the bad Catholics. You choose who to imitate from among all the people SERMO

of God; Well, if you want to imitate the crowd, you exclude yourself from the few who walk the narrow path. Stay away from theft, fraud and perjury. Far be it from you the abyss of drunkenness! Fear fornication as you fear death; not the death that frees the soul from the body, but that which will make the soul burn forever with the body. I know that the devil will do his part, and will not stop speaking to the hearts of those he drags into his party through seduction. I know that the devil says to the hearts of adulterers and fornicators who are not satisfied with their wives: "The sins of the flesh are of no greater importance." Against this, against this whisper of the devil we must seek the enchantment of Christ. The enemy deceives Christians by using the pleasures of the flesh when he presents what is really serious as unimportant, lying to them instead of telling them the truth. What does it matter that Satan presents it as unimportant, if Christ shows that it has it? What good is it if the enormous weight of unhappiness appears diminished on the scale of falsehood? What good does it do you if the devil tells you that what God says is heavy is light? Aren't you going to experience what God says is heavy? Will you not find far from you the enemy who made you such promises? Is the devil doing something new when he tells the faithful Christians: “It doesn't matter what you do. You sin in the flesh, but not in the spirit. It is easily erased and forgiven"? What is extraordinary about this? It's the same trick he used in paradise: "You will not die." God had said: "On the day you eat,

you will die." The enemy comes and says: “What is it that God told you that you will die? You will not die; but when you eat, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods.” God's threat was ignored and attention was paid to the devil's promise. But God's threat turned out to be true, and the devil's deception false. But what good did it do, I beseech you, what did it do the woman to say: The serpent enticed me; and to the man: The woman whom you gave me as a companion gave to me and I ate? Did the excuse work for them and they avoided the sentence? For this reason, my brothers, my children, I speak to you like this. Those of you who have a wife should not know any other; Those of you who do not have it, but want to have it, remain chaste for them, as you want them to be for you. Those of you who have promised continence, do not look back. I have told you; I am liberated. The Lord put me to give, not to ask for accounts. And yet, when I can, when it is reality and the fact is admitted, when I know it, I correct, I reproach, I give to the anathema and I excommunicate 2. But, nevertheless, I do not get the correction, since neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is something, but God, who gives the growth. And even now, when I speak to you, fill you with terror and exhort you, God must hear me and act in some way in silence in your hearts. nis, a fraudibus, a periuriis abstinete. Gurges ebrietatis repellatur a uobis. Topic: The Incarnate Word. Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Day. 1. The Son of God, born of the Father before time, reveals to us the sublimity of the grace that God has granted us. Suppose we ask that question, although we are not allowed to doubt it. The Lord himself responded to these thoughts when the Jews said to him: You are not yet fifty years old, and have you already seen Abraham? His response was as follows: Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham existed, I existed. So he existed, but not yet as a man. And in case anyone thought he was an angel, the holy gospel told you what Christ was. Do you also ask what it was? In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God. There you have what it was: In the beginning the Word existed. The Word was not created in the beginning, but the Word existed. Although the spirit is ready, as the flesh is weak, I must not detain you too much in the sermon after the fatigue of last night 1; But I must say a few words to you. These days that follow the passion of our Lord, and in which we sing the Hallelujah to God, are for us days of celebration and joy and last until Pentecost, the date on which the promised Holy Spirit was sent from heaven. Of these days, the seven or eight that we are in are dedicated to the sacraments that the newborns have received. Those who until recently were called competent are now called infantrymen. They were called competent because with their request they shook the mother's womb to be born; They are called infants because those who had previously been born for the world have just been born for Christ. Remembering this grace, as you make the liberation from your sins a reality, since it is God who accomplishes it in you, approach with fear and trembling to participate in this altar. Recognize in the bread what hung from the tree, and in the chalice what flowed from the side. In their manifold variety, those ancient sacrifices of God's people figured in this one future sacrifice. that now, he says, I understand. The Father is greater than me. He speaks the manner of a servant; seek the form of God. This is what I said: If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, since the Father is greater than I. When you see me now, you see me in what makes me lesser. If you love me, when you see me in what I am less, you will also see that way in which I am equal. Do you wonder that the Son is less than the Father in the form of a servant? I tell you that he is even less than himself, since he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant. If you consider it said of him: He has been made a little lower than the angels; If you have already set your eyes on the form of a servant, do not remain in it, rise above and confess that Christ is equal to the Father. Why do you hear with so much pleasure: The Father is greater than me? Listen with even greater satisfaction: I and the Father are one. This is the Catholic faith, which navigates as between Scylla and Charybdis, as one navigates in the strait between Sicily and Italy: on the one hand, rocks that cause a shipwreck, and on the other, whirlpools that devour the ships. If the ship hits the rocks, it is destroyed; If it ends up in the whirlpool, it is swallowed up. So also Sabellius, who said: «It is only one; "The Father and the Son are not two." Notice the shipwreck. Also the Arian: "There are two, one greater and one lesser, not equal in essence." Notice the whirlpool. Navigate between the two, keep the path straight. If Catholics are called Orthodox, it is not without reason; "Orthodox" is a Greek word that in Latin is equivalent to "upright." So, if you keep the path straight, you avoid both Scylla and Charybdis. Hold fast to this: The Father and I are one. Me and the Father: listen to him. 5. Being born man from man at a moment in time who was God from God, God to the exclusion of all time; having been born in mortal flesh, in the likeness of sinful flesh; the fact of having gone through infancy, having overcome childhood and having reached maturity factum Verbum, sicut in principle fecit deus caelum et terram: hoc fecit Verbum. 1. Resurrectio domini Iesu Christi forma est christianae fidei. Quod enim natus est ex homine homo certo tempore, deus autem ex deo, sine aliquo tempore deus; quod ergo natus est in carne mortali, in similarityine carnis peccati, quod portavit infantiam, transgressus est pueritiam, pervenit ad iuventutem, et hanc perduxit ad mortem, hoc totum resurrectioní militabat. and having led her to death, all of this was at the service of the resurrection. For he would not have been resurrected if he had not died, and he would not have died if he had not been born; For this reason, the fact of being born and dying existed as a function of the resurrection. That Christ the Lord was born a man of man, many believed, even strangers and impious people, although they were unaware of his virgin birth; that Christ was born as a man, both friends and enemies believed; that Christ was crucified and died, both friends and enemies believed; Only his friends know that he was resurrected. And why this? Christ the Lord, in the act of being born and dying, had his sights set on the resurrection; In it he established the limits of our faith. Our race, that is, the human race, knew two things: being born and dying. To teach us what we did not know, He took what we knewT. In the region of the earth, in our mortal condition, it was common, absolutely common to be born and die; so common that, just as it cannot occur in heaven, so on earth it does not cease to exist. On the other hand, who knew about resurrection and living forever? This is the novelty that was brought to our region by someone who came from God. Great act of mercy!: he became man for man; the creator of man became man! It was nothing extraordinary for Christ to be what he was, but he wanted it to be great to become what he had done. What does it mean to "do what he had done"? Become a man who had made the man. Here is his mercy. esset, nisí natus esset; ac per hoc, quod natus et mortuus est, resurrectioni_ profecít. Natum hominem de homine dominum Christum multi et alieni et impii crediderunt: quamvis de virgine non noverunt, tamen hominem natum crediderunt Christum et amici et inimici, crucifixum et mortuum Christum crediderunt et amici et inimici: resurrexisse non noverunt nisi soli amici. Hoc autem propter quid? Ule autem dominus Christus, quod nasci voluit, quod morí voluit, resurgere intendit: ibi nobis diffinivit fidem. In genere enim nostro, id est, in genere humano duas res noveramus: nasci, et mori. Ut doceret et quod (480) non noveramus, suscepit quod noveramus. Usitatum Fuit in regione terrena, in conditione mortalitatis nostrae, prorsus usitatum Fuit nasci et mori: tam usitatum, ut in cáelo esse non posset, in terra esse non cesset. Resurgere autem, et in aeternum vivere, quís noverat? Hoc novum attulit ad regionem nostram, qui venit ex deo.

Factus est pro homine homo, magna miseratio: factus homo, factor hominis. Non erat magnum Christo esse quod erat: sed magnum esse voluit fieri quod fecerat. Quid est, fieri quod fecerat? Fieri homo, qui hominem fecerat. Haec est miseratio eius.

2. Everything that is done in this life, in which men want to be happy without achieving it... A good thing is what they love so much, but they do not look for what they want in the right place. Everything is given in its place. Even on earth, gold is not found anywhere, nor is silver or lead; The same fruits of the field each come from a different place. As if each region accepted some and rejected others, some fruits are borne in one place and others in another; They are diverse according to different places. The only thing that exists everywhere is birth and death. However, the same birth and death do not occur in the entire creation, but only in this lower stratum; In heaven neither birth nor death occurs from the moment all things were created. Certainly the prince of the angels could have fallen with his companions, but to replace the fallen angels men will go there to occupy the place they left 2. When the devil saw that the man was going to ascend to the place from which he had fallen, he was filled with envy; He fell and knocked down others. What does it mean that the devil fell? What does it mean that he knocked the man down? He conquered everything who did not fall, but descended. Man fell: God descended and became man. Where birth and death abound is the region of misery. Men seek to be happy in the region of misery; They seek eternity in the region of death. The Lord, the truth, tells us: «What you are looking for is not found here, because it is not from here. What you seek is good and every man desires it; 2: Totum quod agitur in ista vita, in qua volunt beati esse homines, et non possunt... Bonum est enim quod valde volunt, sed non in regione sua quaetunt quod cupiunt. Certa quaeque enim in suis regionibus nascuntur. Et in terra non ubique nascitur aurum, non ubique argentum, non ubique plumbum: ipsae fruges aliae alibi proveniunt: sicut quaeque regio tulerit vel recusaverit, alia poma in illo loco, alia in illo et in illo, diverse per diverse; et nihil ubique, nisi nasci et mori. Verumtamen hoc ipsum nasci et mori, non de universe mundo, sed de ista parte Ínfima mundi: in caelis enim non est nasci et mori, ex quo ibi condita sunt omnia. Cadere inde potuit princeps quidem angelorum cum sociis suis; sed pro ipsis qui ceciderunt angelis homines illuc venturi sunt, et implebunt locum eorum qui ceciderunt. Quia ergo diabolus vidit hominem ascensurum unde ipse ceciderat, vidit, et invidit: cecidit, et deiecit.

Sed quid est, quod diabolus cecidit? quid est, quod hominem deiecit? Totum vicit, qui non cecidit, sed descendit. Cecidit homo: descendít deus, et factus est homo. Ubi ergo abundat nasci et mori, regio est miseriae: beati quaerunt esse homines in regione miseriae (481) aeternitatem quaerunt in regione mortis. Ait nobis dominus, ait nobis veritas: Quod quaeritis, non est hic, quia non est hinc. Topic: The appearance of Jesus to the apostles. Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Wednesday (or Monday). 1. The gospel readings on the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ are read solemnly and in a certain order. Today we have heard that Christ the Lord showed his disciples the true flesh in which he had suffered and risen. They heard him speak, they saw him present, and yet they still had to touch him after he told them: Touch, feel, and see that the spirits do not have flesh or bones, as you see that I have. But when they saw it, they doubted and believed they were seeing a spirit, not a body. Whoever still thinks that the resurrection of the Lord was not corporal, but only spiritual, may God forgive him, as he also forgave his apostles!; but only if they do not remain in error and change their mind, as they also heard it and changed. And how great was his benevolence! Not only did he show himself present to them in his body, but he also strengthened them with the truth of the Holy Scripture. These are the words, he said to them, that I spoke to you when I was still with you. As? Wasn't he with them then and talking to them? What does it mean then: When SERMO was still

with you? Without a doubt, when he was still mortal with you and like you. These are the words that I spoke to you: that it was fitting that all things that were written about me in the law, in the scriptures, and in the psalms should be fulfilled. Then his intelligence was opened so that they could understand the Scriptures. He is the one who to this day opens to us the Scriptures of life, he who died for us. 2. But let's see what he told them: For it was fitting that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all peoples, beginning at Jerusalem. You see that the disciples not only saw Christ after the resurrection, but they also heard from his mouth that, according to the Holy Scripture, this was how it had to happen. We have not seen Christ present in his flesh, but we listen daily to the Scriptures, with which they were also strengthened. What did he tell them about the Scriptures? Let penitence and forgiveness of sins be preached in his name by all peoples, beginning with Jerusalem. The disciples did not see this; They only saw Christ, who spoke of the future Church. But through the word of Christ they believed what they did not see. They saw the head, but not yet the body; We see the body, but we believe what refers to the head. There are two: the husband and the wife, the head and the body, Christ and the Church. He manifested himself personally to the disciples and promised them the Church; He showed us the Church and ordered us to believe what refers to him. with faith than with the flesh; Touching Christ here is equivalent to touching him with faith. That woman who was suffering from an issue of blood approached him with faith and touched his dress with her hand, but with faith his majesty. See also here what it means to touch. On that occasion only she touched the Lord, crowded by the crowd. Thus he asks: Who touched me? Full of surprise, since the crowd pressed him from all sides, the disciples answered him: The crowd presses you, and you say: "Who touched me?" And he replied: Someone has touched me. When he was with his disciples in his visible flesh and in his palpable bodily substance, he was seen and was touched; but now that he is seated at the right hand of the Father, who among us can touch him? It is true that he is in heaven; It is true that it is far away; It is true that the space that separates it from us cannot be measured. Believe and you touch it. What do I say, do you touch it? Since you believe, you have with you the one in whom you believe. tomb; and cries for him like a man. Oh touch! Oh tangere! Quia ergo videbat eam circa formam servi oceupatam, formam dei, qua aequalis est Patri, nec sapere, nec credere, nec intellegere noverat, differt tactum, ut impleat tactum. Noli me, inquid, tangere, nondum enim ascended ad Patrem meum. Tangís me antequam ascendam ad Patrem, et in solo nomine credis: quid tibi prodest, quod credis? Sine ergo ascendam ad Patrem. 1. De lectione evangelii hodie secundum Iohannem resurrectio dominl recitata est, et audivimus quaesitum esse dominum a discipulis, et non Inventum in sepulchro; hoc autem mulieres nuntiaverunt, non eum (486)

The women had already announced, believing not that he had risen, but that he had been stolen from there. Two disciples arrived, John the Evangelist himself—it is understood that he was the one whom Jesus loved—and Peter with him; They entered, they saw only the bandages, but no body. What is written about John himself? If you have noticed it, it says: He entered, saw and believed. You heard that he believed, but this faith is not praised; In fact, both true things and false things are believed. For if the believer had been praised in this case or faith had been recommended in the fact of seeing and believing, the Scripture would not continue with these words: He did not yet know the Scriptures, according to which it was fitting that Jesus should rise from the dead. So he saw and believed. What did you believe? What did he believe except what the woman had said, namely, that they had taken the Lord from the tomb? She had said: They have taken the Lord from the tomb and I do not know where they have laid him. They ran, entered, saw only the bandages, but not the body, and they believed not that he had risen, but that he had disappeared. They saw him absent from the tomb, they believed that he had been stolen and they left. The woman stayed there and began to look for Jesus' body with tears and to cry next to the tomb. They, stronger for their sex, but with less love, worried less. The woman sought Jesus more insistently, because she was the first who had lost him in paradise; Since death had entered through her, that is why she sought life more. And yet, how did he look for her? She was looking for the body of a dead person, not the incorruption of the living God, since she did not believe that the cause of non-credentes resurrection, sed furto ablatum esse de sepulchro. Quod autem venerunt duo discipuli, Iohannes ipse evangelista — ipse enim intellegitur, quem diligebat Iesus — et cum illo Petras, et ingressi sunt, et viderunt linteamina sola, nullum autem corpus: quid scriptum est de ipso Iohanne? Si advertistis, intravit, ait, et viáit, et credidit (lo 20.8). Hoc quod audistis, credidit, non est fides laudata: creduntur enim et vera et false. Ergo vidit, et credidit: quid ergo credidit? quid credidit, nisi quod mulier dixerat, ablatum esse dominum de sepulchro?

Topic: The miraculous fishing (Jn 21,1-14). Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Friday 412.

1. Your charity knows that every year these readings of the holy gospel are solemnly celebrated, testimonies of the resurrection of the Lord. As reading renews memory, commenting on it also renews it. With the help of the Lord, then, we are going to say what you are used to hearing every year. And if to enhance memory the reading must be repeated, which can be read in the gospel at any other time, how much more reason must the sermon that is heard only once a year be repeated! The Lord appeared to his disciples, after his resurrection, next to the Sea of ​​Tiberias, and found them fishing, but without having caught anything. They achieved nothing in a whole night of fishing; But the day shone, and then they made captures, because they saw the day, Christ, and they let down their nets in the name of the Lord. There are two things we find the disciples having done in the name of Christ; the first when he chose them and made them apostles; the second now, after his resurrection from the dead. Let us compare them, if you like, and let us carefully consider the differences between one and the other, since they have something to do with the construction of our SERMO

Topic: "Simon, do you love me?" (Jn 21,15-25). Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Saturday. From 410. 1. See that the Lord, appearing to the disciples for the second time after the resurrection, subjects the apostle Peter to an interrogation, and forces him to confess his love in triplicate to whom he denied him three other times. Christ was resurrected in the flesh, and Peter in the spirit, for as Christ had died in his passion, so Peter in his denial. Christ the Lord rises from the dead, and with his love he resurrected Peter. He found out the love of the one who confessed it, and entrusted his sheep to him. What did Peter give to Christ by loving him? If Christ loves you, the benefit is for you, not for Christ; and, if you love Christ, the benefit is also for you, not for Christ. However, wanting to show Christ the Lord where men should show that they love Christ, he entrusted his sheep to him. He made this quite clear: —Do you love me? -I love you. fiunt centum viginti: adde sedecim, fiunt centum triginta sex: adde decem et septem, fiunt centum quinquaginta three. —Feed my sheep. And so once, twice and three times. He did not respond but that he loved him; The Lord did not ask him about anything else but his love; He entrusted nothing to the one who answered him but his sheep. Let us also love, and so we love Christ. Christ, in fact, God from always, was born as a man in time. As a man born of men, he appeared to men; As God in man, he did frequent wonderful works. As a man he suffered many evils at the hands of men; as God in man, he was resurrected after death. As a man, he lived on earth for forty days with men; as God in man ascended to heaven in his presence and is seated at the right hand of the Father. We believe all this, we do not see it; and we are commanded to love Christ the Lord, whom we do not see; and we all proclaim and say: "I love Christ." If you do not love your brother, whom you see, how can you love God, whom you do not see? Show that you have love for the shepherd by loving the sheep, because the sheep are also members of the shepherd. So that the sheep could become his members, he himself deigned to become a sheep; so that the sheep could be his members, he was led to the sacrifice like a sheep; so that the sheep would become his members, it was said of him: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. But great is the strength of this lamb. Do you want to know how much strength he showed he had? The lamb was crucified and the lion was defeated. See and consider with what power Christ the Lord rules the world, if by his death he conquered the devil. (lo 21,15-17). Hoc semel, hoc secundo, hoc tertio. Nihil aliud ille responder, quam amare se: nihil aliud dominus interrogat, utrum amaret eum: nihil aliud responderti commendavit, nisi oves suas. Amemus nos, et Christum amamus. Christus enim, deus semper, homo ex tempore natus est. Ut homo de nomine, apparuit homo hominíbus; fecit fines mirabilia, ut deus in homine. Passus est fines mala, ut homo ab hominibus; resurrection post mortem, ut deus in homine. Conversatus est in terra quadraginta diebus, ut homo cum hominibus; ante oculos eorum ascendit in caelum, ut deus in homine, sedet ad dexteram Patris. Totum hoc creditnus, non videmus: et iubemur amare (493) dominum Christum, quem non videmus: et omnes clamamus, et dicimus, Amo Christum.

Si fratrem quem vides non diligis, deum quem non vides quomodo diligere potes? (2 lo 4,20) Amando oves, ostende amorem habere pastoris; nam et ipsae oves membra sunt pastoris. Ut membra eius essent oves, ovis esse dignitus est: ut membra eius essent oves, sicut ovis ad immolandum ductus est (Is 53,7): ut membra eius essent oves, de illo dictum est, ecce agnus dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi (lo 1,29). Sed magna in isto agno fortitudo. Vis nosse, quanta apparuit in isto agno fortitudo? Crucifixus is agnus, et victus is leo. Videte et consider yourself, qua virtute dominus Christus mundum regit, qui morte sua diabolum vicit.

2. Let us love him, then; We hold nothing in greater esteem. Do you think, perhaps, that the Lord does not ask us the same question? Did only Pedro deserve to be subjected to that interrogation and not us? When that reading is read, every Christian suffers the questioning in his heart. Consequently, when you listen to the Lord, who says: Peter, do you love me?, think of him as a mirror and look at yourself. Well, what was Peter if not a figure of the Church? Thus, when the Lord questioned Peter, he questioned us, he questioned the Church. So that you notice that Peter was a figure of the Church, remember that place in the gospel: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not overcome it; I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven. It is only one man who receives them. He himself indicated what the keys to the kingdom of heaven are: What you bind on earth will also be bound in heaven, and what you loose on earth will also be loosed in heaven. If this was said to only one Peter, only Peter did it; Once he is dead or gone, who binds, who unties? I dare say that we also have these keys. What am I saying? That we also bind and loose? You also bind and loose, for whoever is bound is separated from your company, and when he is separated from your company, he is bound by you. In the same way, when he is reconciled, he is loosed by you, since you also pray to God for him. 2. Amemus ergo illum, nihil nobis sit eo carius. Putatis ergo quia nos non interrogat dominus? Petrus solus meruit interrogan, et non nos? Quando illa lectío legítur, unusquisque Christianus interrogatur in corde suo. Quando ergo audis dominum dicentem. Petre, do you love me? speculum puta, et attends ibi te. Nam quid aliud ipse Petrus quam figuram gerebat ecclesiae? Dominus ergo quando Petrum interrogabat, nos interrogabat, ecclesiam interrogabat. Nam ut sciatis Petrum figuram ecclesiae portasse, locum illum evangelii recolite: tu es Petrus, et [581] super hanc petram aedificabo ecclesiam meam; et portae inferorum non vincent eam: tibi dabo keys regni caelorum (Mt 16,18-19). Unus homo accipit. Quae sint enim keys regni caelorum, ipse exposuit: quae ligaveritis in terra, erunt ligata et in cáelo; et quae solveritis in tena, soluta erunt et in cáelo (Mt 16,19). Si uni Petro dictum est, solus hoc fecit Petrus: obiit, et abiit; quis ergo ligat, quis solvit?

Audeo dicere, keys istas habemus et nos. Et quid dicam? Quia nos ligamus, nos solvimus? Ligatis et vos, solvitis et vos. Qui enim ligatur, a vestro consortio separatur: et cum a vestro consortio separatur, a vobis ligatur: et quando reconciliatur, a vobis solvitur, quia et a vobis deus pro illo rogatur. The separation of the "penitents" had Play in the church, in that they occupied a separate place; but also in ordinary life, since the other Christians stopped eating with them (Comments on the mimas 100,8; Reply to the letter of Varmeniano III 2,13). Note, on the other hand, how Augustine wants to emphasize the role of the entire community in the reconciliation of penitents.

3. We all, then, love Christ and are his members. When he entrusts the sheep to the shepherds, the total number of shepherds is reduced to the body of the one shepherd. And so that you may know that the entire number of shepherds is reduced to the body of the one shepherd, Peter is certainly a shepherd, shepherd without a doubt; shepherd is also Paul, shepherd without a doubt; shepherd is Juan, Santiago, Andrés; shepherds are the remaining apostles. All holy bishops are certainly pastors, no one doubts it. And how is this true: And there will be one flock and one shepherd? If, indeed, it is true that there will be one flock and one shepherd, the entire countless number of shepherds is reduced to the body of the one shepherd. But you are also in it; you are its members. Their members were trampled by that Saul, first a persecutor, then a preacher, eager to kill and destroy the faith when the head cried out in favor of its members. All his fury was broken with a single sentence. Which? Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? Could Paul throw even a stone into heaven, where Jesus sits? Let us grant that Saul would have been among the crowd when Jesus was hanging from the tree. Let us admit that Saul would also have shouted with the crowd: 'Crucify him, crucify him'.; and that he was counted among those who, shaking their heads and insulting him, said: If he is the Son of God, let him come down from the cross. Admitting all that, what did it do to him who was sitting in heaven? What word could harm him, what scream, what wood, what spear? Nothing could be done to him now, and yet he cried out:

Why are you chasing me? When he cried out: Why are you persecuting me?, he was indicating that we are his members. Therefore, the love of Christ, whom we love in you; The love of Christ, whom you also love in us in the midst of temptations, fatigue, sweat, worries, miseries and groans, will lead us to the place where there is no fatigue, no misery, no groaning, no sighing, no discomfort; where no one is born, no one dies, no one fears the wrath of the powerful by clinging to the face of the almighty.

3. Omnes enim Christum amamus, membra ipsius sumus; et cum ille commendat oves pastoribus, redigitur totus numerus pastorum ad corpus unius pastoris. Nam ut noveritis omnem numerum pastor(494,)rum redigi ad unum corpus unius pastoris, certe pastor Petrus, plañe pastor: pastor Paulus, ita sane pastor: Iohannes pastor, Iacobus pastor, Andreas pastor, et ceteri apostoli pastors. Omnes sancti episcopi sunt certe pastors, ita plane. Et quomodo verum est, et erit unus grex et unus pastor (lo 10,16)? Porro si verum est, Erit unus grex et unus pastor, omnis innumerabilis pastorum numerus ad corpus unius pastoris redigitur. Be ibi estis et vos, membra ipsius estis. Ipsa membra conculcabat, quando caput pro suis membris clamabat, Saulus ille ante persecutor postea praedicator, Anans caedem, differens fidem. Una voce postratus est totus eius Ímpetus. What voice? Saule, Saule, why are you after me? (Act 9,4) Numquid Saulus vel lapidem posset mittere ad caelum, ubi sedet Iesus? This was Saulus in peat, when Iesus pendebat in ligno. This dixerit et Saulus cum turba, crucijige, crucijige (Luke 23:21); et fuerit inter illos, qui caput agitabant insulting, et dicebant, si filius dei est, descendat de cruz (Mt 27,40-42). Sedenti in cáelo quid faceret? quid noceret verbum? What is the clamor? quid noceret iignum? quid noceret lancea? Nihil ei iam fieri poterat, et tamen clamabat: You persecute me. When I cried out: You persecute me, membra sua

nos esse indicabat. Amor itaque Christi, quem amamus in vobis: amor Christi, quem vos quoque amatis in nobis, inter temptatíones, inter labors, inter sweats, inter sollicítudines, inter miserias, inter gemitus, perducet nos, ibi nullus est labor, nulla miseria, nullus gemitus, nullum [582] suspirium, nulla discomfort, nemo nascítur, nemo moritur, nemo timet iram potentis, haerendo vultui omnipotentis. Topic: "Simon, do you love me?" (Jn 21,15-25). Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Saturday. After 410. 1. You have heard the confession of the apostle Peter when the Lord asked him, as you heard before his denial when the maid terrified him. Full of presumption, he had been assured: "You will deny me"; full of love, he was asked: Do you love me? The reason why the apostle Peter hesitated is that he had previously boasted of the strength of his soul. The psalm had already said it previously: Those who trust in their courage. Peter had become like him of whom it is sung in the Psalms: I said in my abundance: "I will never move." In

1. Audistis apostoli Petri domino interrogante confessionem, cuius audieratis negationem ancilla terrente. Dictum enim erat praesumenti, Negabis me; dictum est diligenti, Do you love me? Ut enim titubaret apos'tolus Petrus, praesumpsit de viribus animi sui. Tam vero olim dixerat psalmus: qui confidunt in virtute sua...(Ps 48,7). Factus ergo erat Petras tamquam ille, de quo cantatur in psalmis: ego dixi in abundantia mea

His abundance had said to Christ: I will go with you to death; In his abundance he had said: I will never move. But the Lord, as a doctor and doer, knew better than the sick person himself what was happening in the sick person. Doctors do, with respect to bodily illnesses, what the Lord can also do with respect to illnesses of the soul. In fact, what do you think, I beg you, of the sick person having to wait for the doctor to tell him what is happening to him? He can personally know the pains he suffers; but their danger, their causes, the possibility of getting out of them or not, no; The doctor takes the pulse and tells the patient what is happening in the patient himself. Thus, when the Lord said to Peter: You will deny me three times, he listened to the vein of his heart. You see that what the doctor predicted came true and what the patient presumed turned out to be false. There, in the same psalm, the Holy Spirit continues: I said in my abundance: "I will never move," as one who boasts of the strength of his soul. Then he added: Lord, by your will you gave strength to my beauty. You turned away your face, and I was filled with confusion. What did he say? «What I had I had received from you, but I believed it was from me. You turned away your face: you took back what you had given me, and I was filled with confusion. When you walked away, I discovered who I am. The Lord temporarily separated himself from Peter to make him healthily humble; but when he looked at her, he cried. non movebor in aeternum (Ps 29,7). In abundantia sua dixerat Christo, tecum usque ad mortem (Luke 22:33); in abundantia sua dixerat, Non movebor in aeternum. Dominus tamen tamquam medicus artifex, quid in infirmo ageretur, melius noverat, quam ipse infirmus. Faciunt hoc medici in valtitudinibus corporum, quod dominus potest etiam in valtitudinibus animarum. Nam quid tibi videtur, rogo te, ut expectet aeger a medico audire quid in illo agatur? Ipse enim dolors quos patitur potest nosse; utrum autem periculosi sint, et quas causa habeant, utrum inde possit aut non possit evadere, medicus venam inspicit, et quid in aegroto agatur ipse aegroto renuntiat. Quando ergo dominus blessed Petro ter me negabis (Mt 26:34) says bat, venam cordis eius tangebat. Ecce factum est quod (496) praedixit medicus, et falsum inventum est quod praesumsit aegrotus. Ibi enim in eodem psalmo sequitur Spiritus sanctus: ego dixi in abundantia mea, non movebor in aeternum, quasi praesumens de viribus animi sui.

Continuous subiecit: dominate, in voluntate tua praestitisti decori meo virtutem. Avertisti jaciem tuam, et factus sum conturbatus (Ps 29,8). Quid dixit? Quod habebam, abs te habebam, et a me esse credebam. Avertisti faciem tuam, tulisti quod dederas; et factus sum conturbatus. Inveni qui eram, quia tu recesseras. Dominus ergo Petrum, ut salubriter humilem faceret, ad tempus deseruit: ta[583]men quando illum respexit,
See supplementary note 24: Christ the Physician p.801.

This is how you find it in the gospel. After having denied him three times and after what was predicted by the Lord has been fulfilled... what is written? The Lord looked at him, and Peter remembered. If the Lord had not turned his gaze on him, Peter would have completely forgotten. The Lord looked at him, and Peter remembered that Jesus had said to him: "Before the rooster crows, you will have denied me three times." And he went out and wept bitterly. Peter needed the baptism of tears to wash away the sin of his denial; but how could he obtain it if the Lord did not give it to him? That is why the apostle Paul says when he warned the people about how they should behave with some who think differently: Gently correct those who think differently, in case God grants them repentance. Thus, penance is also a gift from God. Hard ground is the heart of a proud man; He does not soften to penitence if the grace of God does not rain down. 2. Now, after the resurrection of the Lord, Peter is subjected to an interrogation: his confession is obtained and his martyrdom is predicted; He is found anchored in charity and strengthened in virtue. Already after the resurrection the Lord says to him: «Peter, do you love me more than these? You who denied me, do you love me? Enough things have already happened: you see in life someone you saw go to death when you feared dying. Look, I'm alive, it's me; why were you afraid to die? When you denied me, that didn't mean you lost me. Therefore, since I am myself, do you love me? And he: «Lord, you also know that you feel flevit. Sic enim habes in gospel: postea quam ter negavit, et impletum est quod praedixerat dominus, quid setiptum est? Respexit eum dominus, et rememberatus est Petrus. Si dominus non respexisset, totum Petrus oblitus Fuisset. Respexit eum dominus, et recordatus est Petrus, quia dixerat ei Iesus: antequam gallus cantet, ter me negabis. Et egressus joras flevit amare (Luke 22:61-62). Opus erat ergo Petro ad abluendum negationis peccatum baptismo lacrimarum: sed unde hoc haberet, nisi et hoc dominus daret? Ideo apostólas Paulus eum quibusdam diverse sentientibus ammoneret populum, quemadmodum eum illis agere debenent, ait: In lenitate currents diverse sentientes, ne forte det illis deus paenitentiam. Ergo et paenitentia donum dei est. Dura terra est superientis cor: ad paenitentiam non mollescit, nisi dei gratia compluatur. 2.

Mode ergo iam post domini resurrectionem interrogatur Petrus: elicitur confessio, praedicitur passio: invenitur in caritate, firmatur in virtute. Dicit ei dominus iam post resurrectionem: Petre, diligis me plus his? (lo 21,15) You who denied me, did you interrogate me? Iam satis tibi factum est: vivum vides, quem moríentem vidisti, quando mori timuisti. Ecce vivo, ecce ego sum: quare mori timuisti? When I refused, you identified me as not lost. Ergo diligis me? quia ego sum. Et ille: domine, etiam, tu six quia amo te (lo 21,15). Why are you asking me what six? Sciebas,

3. He is prepared for more sublime and greater things; It is said to him: Feed my sheep, where their flesh will be endangered, but their spirit will be glorified. Indeed, how much he was not going to suffer for the name of Christ in the office of feeding the sheep! Feed my sheep, feed my lambs. Since you love me, what can you give me? The prince of shepherds appointed him a shepherd so that he, Peter, would feed Christ's sheep, not his own. The apostles themselves converted some who wanted to be their followers to common sense. They were sheep of Christ and they wanted to be sheep of men, and one and another said: I am of Pablo, I of Apollo, I of Cejas. There were also sheep who recognized the Lord: I, however, belong to Christ. Paul, knowing that Christ entrusted his own sheep to the apostles, not theirs, rejected such dominion; to be with the Lord, he confesses that he is not the Lord. Does it

Was Paul crucified for you? Or have you been baptized in the name of Paul? You are sheep of Christ, don't you know? Read the sign with which you have been marked. Feed my sheep. Because? Since you love me, since you have affection for me, I entrust my sheep to you; Feed them, but do not forget that they are mine. The leaders of heresies want to make Christ's sheep their own; but, whether they like it or not, they are forced to put the mark of Christ on them; They make them their own patrimony, but they give them the name of the Lord. What does the divine Scripture say in the Song of Songs to those who act like this? The Catholic Church in the midst of heresies. Look how he threatens her. If you do not know yourself: who you are, what you believe, to whom you belong, where you are spread, with what blood you have been redeemed; If you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women! If you do not know yourself, I will expel you, you go out. What does salt you mean? What John says in his letter: They came out from among us, but they were not ours. You go out in the footsteps of the flocks; not in the footsteps of the shepherd, but of the flocks; following in the footsteps of men, not those of Christ. And feed your goats, not my sheep, like Peter. Feed your goats, where? In the shepherds' tents; scattered in the shepherds' tents, not in that of the only shepherd. I also have other sheep. They are not from this fold. It is convenient that I

quando mihi negaturum me praedicebas. Quod ego nesciebam in me, sciebas: et quod scio, rieseis? Armatur ad potiora adque maiora: dicitur ei, stroll oves meas; ubi utique erat periclitaturus in carne, glorificandus in spiritu. Nam pascendo oves Christi, quanta erat pro nomine Christi passurus! love. Why are you asking me what you already know? You knew it when you predicted that I was going to deny you. You knew what I didn't know about myself, and are you going to ignore what I know? Let us do, with your help, what we have just sung to our Lord. The Lord has made all the days; but not without reason has it been written with reference to one in particular: This is the day that the Lord has made. We read that when God created heaven and earth, he said, Let there be light, and there was light. And God called the light day, and the darkness night. But there is another special day for us that must be particularly taken into account, of which the Apostle says: Let us walk honorably as in the day. This common, everyday day lasts from sunrise to sunset. There is another day in which the word of God shines in the hearts of the faithful and expels darkness not from the eyes, but from bad habits. Let us recognize it, then, and rejoice in it. Let us listen to the Apostle, who says: We are, in fact, children of light and children of God; We are not of the night or the darkness. Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in feasting or drunkenness, no, in affairs or impudence, not in quarrels or envy; but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not give yourselves to the care of the flesh, satisfying its lusts. Topic: The disciples of Emmaus (Luke 24:13-35). Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Monday.

1. Yesterday night, the resurrection of the Savior was read according to the gospel of Matthew. Today, as you have heard from the reader, we have been read again, but according to the story of the evangelist Luke. It is often necessary to warn you, something you should not forget, that you do not have to worry if an evangelist says something that another overlooks, since whoever overlooks that one, says something else that the first one had omitted. But there are things that only one evangelist narrates, leaving the other three silent; Others are recorded by two, while the other two remain silent; We found some in three of them, missing only one. Since only one spirit speaks in the four evangelists, the authority of the holy gospel is so great that even what is said by one is true. What you have just heard, that the Lord, after being resurrected, found two of his disciples on a trip, chatting about what had happened, and asked them: What is the topic of conversation that concerns you?, etc., is only narrated by the evangelist Luke. Mark mentions it briefly when he says that he appeared to two who were going

The disciples of Emmaus

journey, but he ignored both what they said to the Lord and what the Lord answered them. 2. What does this reading offer us? Something truly great, if we understand it. Jesus appeared to them. They saw him with their eyes, but they did not recognize him. The teacher walked with them along the way and he himself was the way. Those disciples were not yet on the road, because he found them outside of it. Being with them before the passion, he had predicted everything to them: that he would suffer the passion, that he would die and that on the third day he would rise again. He had predicted everything, but his death erased it from his memory. When they saw him hanging from the tree, they were so upset that they forgot what he had taught them; The resurrection did not cross their minds nor did they remember its promises. We, they say, hoped that he would swear to redeem Israel. You expected it, oh disciples! Are you no longer waiting for it? See that Christ lives: has hope died in you? Christ certainly lives. Christ, alive, finds dead the hearts of the disciples, to whose eyes he appeared and did not appear. They saw it and it remained hidden from them. In fact, if they did not see him, how did they hear him when he asked and how did they answer him? He went with them as a traveling companion and he himself was the guide. Without a doubt, they saw him, but they did not recognize him. Their eyes, as we heard, were clouded, which prevented them from recognizing him. They were not troubled to see it, but to recognize it. 3. Attention, brothers; where did he want me to recognize him?

Ran? In the breaking of bread. We have no doubt: we break bread and recognize the Lord. Thinking of us, that we were not going to see him in the flesh, but that we were going to eat his flesh, he did not want to be recognized except there. The breaking of bread is a cause of consolation for every believer, whoever he may be; for everyone who bears the name of Christian, but not in vain; for everyone who enters the church, but with a reason; for everyone who listens to the word of God with fear and hope. The absence of the Lord is not absence. Have faith, and he whom you do not see will be with you. When the Lord spoke to them, they did not even have faith, since they did not believe that He had risen, nor did they have hope that He could do so. They had lost faith and hope. When they were dead, they walked with the living; The dead walked with life itself. Life walked with them, but life did not yet reside in their hearts. You too, then, if you want to possess life, do what they did to recognize the Lord. They welcomed him as a guest. The Lord had the appearance of one who was going far, but they held him back. When they reached the place to which they were going, they said to him: Stay here with us, for the day is already declining. Give him hospitality, if you want to recognize him as a savior. Hospitality restored to them what unbelief had deprived them of. Thus, then, the Lord made himself present in the breaking of the bread. 1. As the Apostle says, our Lord Jesus Christ died for our sins and rose again for our justification. His death is our sowing, and his resurrection our germinating. His death, in effect, means the death of our life. Listen to the Apostle about it: We have been buried with Christ by baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead, so we too might walk in newness of life. He had nothing to repair on the cross, since he ascended it without any sin. Let us repair ourselves to his cross, nailing to it the evil that we have contracted, so that we can be justified by his resurrection. You must distinguish the two things: He was delivered for our sins and was resurrected for our justification. He did not say: "He was delivered for our justification and was resurrected for our crimes." His surrender sounds like sin, and his resurrection sounds like justice. Ergo ne in aliquo eorum erremus, tanquam matrimoniales eorum Evangelii tabulas audiamus. That is, the Apollinarians. Agustín frequently talks about them in his work, but the data he provides are not uniform. According to some texts, the Apollinarians defended that Christ lacked a human soul, that is, his person was formed by the Word and the flesh; According to others, they affirmed that Christ had a soul, but not a rational one, since the Word stood in for the mind, intelligence and reason. Sometimes, Augustine speaks of an evolution of his thought and on other occasions he distinguishes two, three or even four different groups. See Bibliothcque Augustinienne 72; complementary note 30 p.765-767. Soteriological principle applied universally, especially in the Arian and Apollinarian controversy: what was not assumed by Christ was not saved. Therefore, if Christ saved the whole man, he assumed the whole man. See supplementary note 27 of vol. VII p.753: The marriage "tables."

Ecce Deus dat securitatem diis a se factis: securitatem illis dat immortalitatis; securitatem illis dat, quod non relinquant globos corporum suorum. Certe corpus est omne fugiendum? Iamvero quid et ipsi dicant de resurrectione corporum quasi acute, ut non eis, sicut arbitrantur, etiam I will answer us possimus, multum est ut hodie vobis dicam. Sed quia semel promisi vobis, per istos dies istam de resurrectione carnis quaestionem esse versandam, ad ea quae restant, adiuvante Domino, et aures et corda in crastinum praeparate. The quote is taken from Timaeus XI 40 according to Cicero's translation. The text appears again in The City of God XII 26 and XIII 16,1.

Topic: Appearance to the apostles (Luke 24:36-53). Location: Hippo. Date: Easter Wednesday. Between 405 and 410. 1. Let us talk about the resurrection of the flesh, to the extent of our possibilities and the grace that God grants us, on these sacred dates when you celebrate the resurrection of the Lord. Such, indeed, is our faith; such is the gift that we have promised in the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ; He preceded us as an example. He not only wanted to announce to us, but also show us what he has promised us for the end. Those who were with him then saw him, and, as they had been frightened, believing they were before a spirit, they felt the solidity of the body. He not only spoke to their ears with words, but also to their eyes with his presence; But it would have been little to allow himself to be seen if he had not also offered to be touched and felt. He tells them, in effect: Why are you troubled and why do these thoughts rise to your heart? They thought they were seeing a spirit. Why are you troubled, he said to them, and why do these thoughts rise to your heart? See my hands and my feet; Feel and see, that the spirits do not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have. Against such great evidence, SERMO
IN DIEBUS PASCHALIBUS, XIII

De Resurrectione corporum, against Gentiles CAPUT I.—1. Resurrectionis fides mani[H39]festo probata, imprudenter ab hominibus impugnatur.—Diebus his sanctis resurrectioni Domini dedicatis, quantum donor ipso possumus, de carnis resurrectione tractemus. Haec enim fides est nostra, hoc donum in Domini nostri Iesu Christi nobis carne promissum est, et in ipso praecessit exemplum. Voluit enim nobis quod promisit in fine, non solum praenuntiare, sed etiam demonstrare. lili quidem qui tune fuerunt cum illo, víderunt, et cum expavescerent, et spiritum se videre crederent, soliditatem corporis tenuerunt. Locutus est enim non solum verbis ad aures eorum, sed etiam specie ad oculos eorum: parumque erat se praebere cernendum, nisi etiam offerret pertractandum atque palpandum. Ait enim: Quid turbati estis, et cogitationes ascendant in cor vestrum? Putaverunt enim se spiritum videre. Quid turbati estis, inquit, et cogitationes ascendant in cor vestrum? Videte manus meas et pedes meos; Pálpate, et videte, quia spiritus ossa et carnem non habet, sicut me videtis habere (Luke 24,38.39). Contra istam evidentiam disputant homines. Quid enim aliud facerent

men still start arguing! What else can men who derive pleasure from nothing but human things do but argue about God, but against God? But he is God, and they, however, are men. God knows the thoughts of men, and knows that they are vain. The carnal man has no other standard to understand than what he is used to seeing. They believe what they usually see; What they don't usually see they don't believe. God, precisely because he is God, performs miracles that are out of the ordinary. But the fact that so many men are born daily who did not exist before is certainly a greater miracle than the resurrection of a few who already existed. However, attention is not paid to these miracles, since frequency has made them ordinary. Christ was resurrected: it is an unappealable fact. He had a body, he had flesh, he was hung on a cross, he breathed his last and was placed in the tomb. Whoever lived in it showed it alive. Why do we miss each other? Why not believe it? God is the one who has done it; consider who the author is and eliminate all doubt. 2. Men ask if the fragility of the body that they experience in their flesh must exist after the resurrection of the dead. We answer them no. They reply to us: «If it does not exist, why is it eaten? Or if it is not eaten, why did the Lord eat after the resurrection? We have just heard, when the gospel was read, that in order to show them his bodily presence it seemed little to him to present himself alive to the eyes and hands of homines, qui ea quae sunt hominum sapiunt, quam disputarent de Deo contra Deum? Ule enim Deus est, illi homines sunt. Sed Deus novit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanae sunt (Ps 93:11). In nomine carnali all regulate intellegendi es consuetudo cernendi. Quod solent videre, credunt; quod non solent, non credunt. Praeter consuetudínem facit Deus miracula, quia Deus est. Maiora quidem miracula sunt, all quotidie homines were born who were not, quam paucos resurrected who were; et also is miracula non consideratione comprehensa sunt, sed assiduitate viluerunt. Resurrexit Christus, absolute res est. Corpus erat, caro erat, pependit in cruz, emisit animam, posita est in sepulcro. Exhibit illam vivam, qui vivebat in illa. Quare miramur? Quare non credimus? Deus est qui fecit: consider auctorem, et tolle dubitationem. CAPUT II.—2.

Contra resurrectionem carnis obtendunt: Si corruptío non erit, cur manducabitur?—Quaerunt ergo homines, utrum corruptio ista corporis, quam sentiunt in carne sua,futura sit in resurrectione mortuorum. Dicimus nonfuturam. Respondent nobis: Si corruptio non erit, quare manducabitur? Aut si non manducabitur, quare post resurrectionem Dominus manducavit? Modo Evangelium cum legeretur, audivimus, quia cum exhibitret se vivum oculis manibusque discipulorum suorum, parum illi visum est ad demonstrandam evidentiam corporalem; • This way of reasoning is very common in the Saint. his disciples, but added: Do you have anything here to eat? And they offered him a piece of roast fish and a honeycomb; He ate it and gave them what was left. We are told, then: "If this fragility will not exist after the resurrection, why did Christ the Lord eat?" You have read that he ate; but did you read that he was hungry? If he ate it was because he wanted to, not because he had a need. If I had wanted to eat, I would have needed something. And in turn, in that case, if they had not been able to eat, their strength would have diminished. Did not the angels also eat when our fathers received them as guests, without this meaning that they were subject to any corruption? 3. They still ask: "Will bodies be resurrected with the defects they had when they died?" We answer them no. We are objected: "Why then did the Lord rise again with the scars of his wounds?" What can we answer them except that this was also the result of their free will, not of any necessity. This is how he wanted to resurrect and this is how he wanted to show himself to some who doubted. The scar of the wound on that flesh healed the wound of unbelief. 4. They are still arguing, and they ask us: "Will those who die as children also be resurrected as children?" Or, although they were young when they died, will they be resurrected in their fullness? We do not find this explicitly stated in Scripture. The promise is limited to stating that bodies are to be resurrected incorruptible and immortal. And if they return to thirst addidit: Habetis hic aliquid quod manducetur? Et obtulerunt ei partem pisáis assi, et favum mellis: et manducavit, et relics dedit illis (Luke 24,41-43). If you desideraret manducare, egeret. Rursus si manducare non posset, [1140] minus valeret. Numquid et Angelí, quando suscepti sunt hospitio a patribus nostris, non manducaverunt (cf. Gen 18:1-9; Tob 12:19), et tamen corruptibiles non fuerunt? 3. Sic resurgere voluit, sic se voluit quibusdam dubitantibus exhibite. In illa carne cicatrix vulnerís, sanavit vulnus incredulitatis. CAPUT III.—4. Varvulorum resurrectio qualis.—Adhuc disputant, et quaerunt a nobis: Parvuli qui moriuntur, parvuli resurrecturi sunt? an aetas erit plena reviviscentium, quorum erat parva mororientium? life at their young age and short stature, does that mean that weakness will also accompany them? Because they are small, will they always be lying down, unable to walk? It is accepted as more credible, more probable and more reasonable that they must be resurrected in adulthood, so that they receive as a gift what they would achieve over time. Well, we must not believe that they are going to resurrect in a decrepit, ailing and bent age. Bottom line, remove anything negative and add whatever you want. 5. But you ask: "How will the earthly body be in heaven?" The Gentile philosophers, the most famous of all, whose foolish, or at any rate human, opinions, I have already shown you 2 - in fact, they did not investigate these things with the spirit of God, but on the basis of conjectures of the human heart -, give the greatest importance to this question. They deal with subtlety about the laws of gravity and the order of the elements, and they say - something that we also admit - that this world is ordered in such a way that the earth is what is lowest, at the bottom; secondly, above it, the waters; then comes the air, and fourthly the ether, above all else. The superior element, which they call ether, is, according to them, a liquid and pure fire from which the stars have been formed; Nothing earthly can exist in it, because the laws of gravity do not allow it. If we answered that our bodies will not be in heaven, but rather that they will live on a new earth, we would be bold and daring; moreover, hasi statura pusilla revocatur, numquid et propterea infirmitas revocatur? Si parvi erunt, numquid iacebunt, et ambulare non poterunt? Credibilius tamen accipitur et probabilius et rationabilius, plenas aetates resurrecturas, ¡ut teddatuí muñere, quod accessuram erat tempoie. Non enim credituri sumus etiam senectam resurrecruram anxiousm et curvam. Postremo corruptionem tolle, et quod vis adde. 5. Terrenum corpus quomodo in cáelo erit.—Sed, inquis, quomodo erit terrenum corpus in cáelo?

Philosophi enim Gentium, illi valde magni, quorum vobis iam vel insanas vel certe humano sententias intimavi (quaesierunt quippe ista non spiritu Dei, sed coniectura cordis humani); hinc máxime faciunt quaestionem, tractant subtiliter de momentis ponderum et ordine elementum; et dicunt, quod etiam videmus, mundum sic esse dispositum, ut ima sit terra tanquam in fundo eius, secunda aqua superfundatur terrae, tertius aer vinot, quartus aether cuneta cooperiat. Illud elementum supernum, quod aethera appellant, ignem dicunt esse liquidum etpuram, inde sidera esse formata, ibi nihil posse esse terrenum, quoniam ordo ponderum non admittit. Si dicamus eis nostra corpora in terra nova esse victura, et in cáelo non future; audacter et teréré, immo infideliter dicimus. Credere enim debenmus
